News.title: CalMac ferry evacuated over 'threat' after passenger goes overboard at Ardrossan
News.content:
A CalMac ferry in Scotland has been evacuated after a 'threat' was made by a passenger, with multiple emergency services responding to the incident at Ardrossan harbour

A ferry on Scotland's west coast was evacuated after a passenger went overboard and allegedly made "threats" against the vessel, sparking a major emergency response at Ardrossan harbour.

Ferry operator CalMac said a person was reported overboard from its MV Caledonian Isles during the 4.40pm sailing from Brodick on the Isle of Arran to Ardrossan. The person was rescued from the water by the ferry's crew.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "Around 5.45pm on Friday, 21 August, 2026, we were made aware that a man had gone overboard the vessel and had caused a disturbance and made threats when he was rescued by staff.

"Officers attended and a 23-year-old man has been arrested in connection with the incident. Enquiries are ongoing. It has been established that the threats made were not credible."

CalMac, the UK's largest ferry operator, operates 29 routes across Scotland's west coast.

News.title: Police issue statement after 'Cat in the Hat' character pictured lurking on streets
News.content:
Police issue statement after 'Cat in the Hat' character pictured lurking on streets

Viral images showing a live-size version of the the Dr Seuss character have caused alarm and fear

View 3 Images Police have had to step in after this image went viral online

Police have issued a statement after terrifying images appeared to show an unknown figure dressed as Dr Seuss' Cat in the Hat terrorising a local neighbourhood.

‌



The creepy images, which first emerged in Limerick, Ireland, showed a freaky cat-like man eerily wandering the streets at night, standing in driveways, and causing alarm among residents. However Gardaí officials said the pictures are not real, and have confirmed instead they were artificially generated by an unknown prankster.

‌



The images first appeared on Facebook, although at the time they were rumoured to have originated on Snapchat, and were accompanied by false and misleading reports that police were investigating the creepy cartoon characters appearance.

‌



The hoax was not just limited to Limerick, with fake images of the black and white feline emerging in the likes of Glanmire, Cork, in Cahir, Tipperary, in Curracloe, Wexford, and Broadford Park in Dublin adding to the hysteria online.

View 3 Images These pictures caused real alarm (Image: Wexford Gardaí)

A spokesperson for Wexford Garda wrote: "In an unusual turn of events we are hearing a lot about an illusive Dr Seuss character doing the rounds online, apparently causing havoc in neighbourhoods and towns across the country.

‌



"Fortunately, we can rule out the issue, which is essentially an AI prompt that places the character into images/videos of familiar places.

"To be clear, the Cat in the Hat was not in your driveway while you were out and he is not currently hiding out in Curracloe."

View 3 Images Would you be scared if you thought this guy was roaming your neighbourhood? (Image: Instagram/masonrosephoto)

Article continues below

This is not the first time police have had to issue warnings regarding fake AI trends. Last year, cops in the UK got involved after a viral prank involving a fake "AI homeless man" led to a string of police calls from people who had fallen victim to the hoax.

Dorset Police revealed they had received a call from one "extremely concerned parent" who was fooled by their daughter into thinking there was a man in their family home while she was alone, only for the cops to discover the whole thing was an AI prank.

A spokesperson for the force said: "If you receive a message and pictures similar to the above antics from friends or family, please attempt to check it isn't a prank before dialling 999."

News.title: 'Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's return to the UK poses one key question - why now?'
News.content:
For much of the last six years, Harry and Meghan have engaged in a game of battleships from the relative safety of 5,000 miles away. The only issue is, they’ve been the only ones launching the bombs.

Now, suddenly peace has been declared and they’re coming back to the UK to live. As the shockwaves continue to reverberate around the households, from Buckingham Palace to Balmoral, there surely is only one question to be answered: why now?

Has the money - of which there has been bundles shoved into the coffers of two willing participants, ready to spill every minute detail over how awful the royals are - really run out already? Has Prince Harry come to his senses and realised trashing your family for cash isn’t a good look after all? Or have the deals from the streaming giants and tech bros ground to a halt, requiring a grand old reinvention pronto?

I guess any of the above could be true. One thing is for certain: nothing is ever as it seems with the Sussexes.

‌



View 5 Images Harry and Meghan will arrive in the UK within days (Image: @meghan/Instagram)

Queen Camilla will be key figure in Harry and Meghan return to royal life READ MORE :

For a couple who have spent years putting extraordinary distance between themselves and the institution Harry was born into, any reintroduction will be a little awkward. You can’t go round calling your dad, the actual King, an old man; suggesting your mother-in-law is dangerous and those who remain unnamed are a bunch of racists, and expect to be welcomed round for Sunday lunch.

Regardless of what the Sussex spin doctors want to suggest, regarding “multiple reasons” for Harry and Meghan upping sticks and returning to a country Harry deemed too unsafe to bring his family a few months ago, the reasons will be entirely self-serving. Now I’ve never been a fan of Suits, but perhaps reports of Meghan returning to acting in Guy Ritchie’s The Gentlemen on Netflix could be the reason.

Such a gig just might be an added reason to relocate your family for……although has anyone cared to tell them they’ve just missed the best British summer ever?!

‌



The crucial point for Harry, and one he really must now surely realise, is that it is no coincidence that relations have improved for him and his family—well, mainly just him and the King—when he has kept his counsel. No more interviews, no more bad mouthing and certainly no more bombshell books.

View 5 Images King Charles is united with his son and heir Prince William that there will be no half in, half out model for the Sussexes (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

While he has spoken of wanting reconciliation - and even apologies - from his family, not even telling his father of his grand plan to return when he was welcomed into his Highgrove home for tea and cake seems incredibly at odds with such a plan. Whatever the reasons, it is difficult to imagine a clearer illustration of just how fractured relations remain between the two camps.

‌



The King, to his credit, appears to have gritted his teeth and accepted the situation. For a father and grandfather, there will inevitably be genuine happiness at the prospect of seeing Archie and Lilibet more often.

But again, everything brings us back to one question which cannot simply be brushed aside. What exactly is driving this? Is it family? A desire to reconnect with Britain? Or something rather more calculated?

The Sussexes have built a hugely lucrative life in America since walking away from royal duties. They have signed multimillion-pound commercial deals, produced television programmes, published books and given interviews which have laid bare their grievances with the Royal Family. But the sheen has undoubtedly faded.

View 5 Images Many members of the royal family believe Harry and Meghan can not be forgiven for raising allegations of racism in their interview with Oprah Winfrey

‌



Having recently spent time in California, I was struck by how little of the extraordinary fascination with the Sussexes that once existed appears to remain. That is anecdotal, of course, and America is a vast country. But conversations I had with Californians and people from elsewhere in the US suggested a striking lack of enthusiasm for the couple.

The question, therefore, is whether Britain represents a new opportunity. Could Meghan's lifestyle ambitions benefit from a European launch? Could Harry see a future in which Britain becomes a more important part of his family's life? Or do they genuinely believe there is an appetite among the British public for their return to royal life?

That last possibility would surely be the most explosive. Because there is one thing the King and his heir appear to have been united on: there can be no return to a "half-in, half-out" model of royal life.

‌



And that is where the problem becomes almost impossible to solve. How could Harry and Meghan simply walk back into the institution they have spent years attacking?

They have accused members of the Royal Family of abandonment, made deeply damaging allegations and publicly discussed claims of racism. Those accusations have not simply disappeared because time has passed. Forgiveness is one thing. Rebuilding trust is another.

View 5 Images The Prince and Princess of Wales want no part in the Sussex drama, sources close to the couple have said (Image: PA)

‌



And then there is the Prince and Princess of Wales. William and Catherine have endured an extraordinary couple of years, from the Princess's cancer battle to the increasing pressure on William as the King's own health problems have brought the reality of his future role into sharper focus. They have emerged from that period looking more resilient than ever.

Whatever their private feelings about Harry and Meghan's latest plans, there is little reason to believe they will allow the future of the monarchy to be derailed. William's position is particularly important. He is not simply Harry's older brother anymore. He is the heir to the throne.

Any decision about bringing the Sussexes back into the royal fold would ultimately have consequences for the institution he will one day inherit. And that is why this seemingly simple decision about where two children go to school could become something much bigger.

The King may want reconciliation. He may desperately want a closer relationship with his grandchildren. But if reconciliation turns into a demand for a renewed royal role, the stakes change dramatically.

‌



After six years of conducting their most damaging battles from an ocean away, Harry and Meghan are potentially bringing themselves – and all the unresolved tensions that come with them – right back into the heart of the Windsor family.

Whatever happens next, one thing feels almost certain. The fireworks have not gone away. They have merely moved considerably closer.

News.title: Woman, 19, raped on Bournemouth seafront had desperately fought her attacker
News.content:
Woman, 19, raped on Bournemouth seafront had desperately fought her attacker

Mohammed Abdullah, 19, has been jailed for raping a 19-year-old woman in a terrifying attack in a Bournemouth seafront toilet

View 2 Images The attack took place on Bournemouth seafront (file) (Image: Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

A teenage predator has been jailed for raping a 19-year-old woman in a portable toilet on Bournemouth seafront as she desperately fought to escape.

Mohammed Abdullah, 19, who was living in the West Drayton area in Middlesex, has been jailed for six years and nine months after being found guilty by a jury at Bournemouth Crown Court of rape and sexual assault. The "terrifying" attack took place in the early hours of July 6, 2025.

In addition to the prison sentence, Abdullah will be placed on the sex offenders register for life.

Mark Eldridge, prosecuting, told the trial that the complainant had been out with a friend that night, firstly in Charminster then moving on to Bar So in Bournemouth, Dorset.

View 2 Images Mohammed Abdullah has been jailed for six years and nine months (Image: Dorset Police/PA Wire)

He said that after having had a "fair amount to drink" she and her friend headed off in different directions and the complainant began walking home along the seafront where she came across the defendant who was with friends and who then offered to give her a lift home on his e-bike.

They then stopped at a portable toilet where Abdullah sexually assaulted her before raping her.

Mr Eldridge said: "She was wriggling and trying to fight and then thought if she let it happen it would be quicker." He added: "The defendant kissed her aggressively and she pulled away but somehow got a burst lip."

He said that following the attack, the defendant rode off while the complainant "took her shoes off in order to run". She then sought help from passers-by, asking to use their phones to call her mother who she told she had been raped. Mr Eldridge said one man who helped her described her as "appearing distressed".

Abdullah arrived in the UK from Syria in 2023 and was given permanent leave to remain under a family reunion scheme.

He previously told the court that the sex was "consensual" and that the complainant had wanted to hug and kiss him.

Detective Inspector Shaun Inkpen, of Dorset Police's Major Crime Investigation Team, said: "Firstly I would like to acknowledge the bravery of the young woman in coming forward and reporting such a horrific and terrifying sexual attack.

"Throughout our investigation and the subsequent criminal justice process she has shown immense strength, courage and resilience. This young woman’s evidence played a crucial role in securing Abdullah’s conviction and subsequent custodial sentence."

Samantha Wright, senior crown prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), said: "Mohammed Abdullah exploited a young woman who was vulnerable and simply trying to get home safely.

"Having gained her trust by offering her a lift, he subjected her to a terrifying sexual attack. The victim’s bravery in reporting what happened and supporting this prosecution has ensured a dangerous offender has been held accountable for his actions.

Article continues below

"Violence against women and girls has no place in our communities. The CPS will continue to work tirelessly to bring perpetrators of these abhorrent offences to justice."

News.title: Glasgow Tesco evacuated as huge blaze sparks 'total panic' and thick smoke pours out
News.content:
Glasgow Tesco evacuated as huge blaze sparks 'total panic' and thick smoke pours out

Customers and staff were evacuated from a Tesco in Glasgow after a fire broke out in its underground car park.

View Image Customers and staff were evacuated from a Tesco in Glasgow

A Tesco store in Glasgow has been evacuated after a fire broke out at the supermarket, sparking “total panic” among shoppers.

The blaze was reported at the supermarket on Maryhill Road at around 4.21pm on Friday, with thick black smoke seen pouring from the car park entrance, reports Glasgow Live.

The fire involved a car which is believed to be electric, while witnesses said staff and customers were evacuated as firefighters tackled the blaze.

Two Scottish Fire and Rescue Service appliances were sent to the scene, with police also in attendance and the car park cordoned off.

One local resident described the scene as “total panic” as the evacuation unfolded. Ryan, 26, an energy consultant who lives opposite the store, told Glasgow Live: “I was just coming home on the bus and I saw the smoke which looked like it was coming out the roof of the Tesco store.

Article continues below

“Then when I rounded the corner to get to my flat I saw it was a car on fire. It looks like an electric car, although I’ve no idea how it started.

“The staff and customers were being evacuated and it was total panic. They are just standing outside now waiting for the firefighters to finish.”

A Scottish Fire and Rescue Service spokesperson said: “We received a call at 4.21pm to reports of a car on fire at the Tesco supermarket on Maryhill Road in Glasgow. We mobilised two appliances and are still at the scene.”

News.title: Kenya helicopter crash: 6 dead as safari 'tourist' chopper crashes in Samburu
News.content:
Six people have been killed after a safari helicopter crashed near Mt Ololokwe in Kenya’s Samburu County, with tourists reportedly on board

A helicopter has crashed near Kirish close to Mt Ololokwe in Kenya’s Samburu County, with all six people on board dead.

A preliminary police report cited by Kenyan newspaper The Star suggested tourists were travelling in the aircraft, although their nationalities have not yet been established and this has not been confirmed.

Local residents and rescue teams were heading towards the scene, where smoke and fire had been seen following the crash.

The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority said the helicopter had been travelling towards the Ewaso Nyiro river, which runs through the Samburu National Reserve, shortly after 9am local time.

A previous version of this article incorrectly reported that "The helicopter was operated by local safari company Tropic Air". We are happy to clarify this and the article has been amended accordingly.

News.title: Mum finds handwritten note at soft play that leaves other parents 'tearing up'
News.content:
Mum finds handwritten note at soft play that leaves other parents 'tearing up'

Often soft play is riddled with chaos and germs, but one mum managed to find something slightly out of place – and it had other parents tearing up at the discovery

View Image Finding a mysterious note can feel quite special (Image: Getty Images)

Parents know the pure chaos which comes with taking their children to soft play. During summer it can be hard finding something for the kids which they won't find boring, so the first thought is taking them to an indoor playground.

‌



With those centres, they're often taken over by kids running and jumping around the place, so finding something out of character would simply not be easy. But one mum managed to discover an item incredibly out of place which nearly left her tearing up. She spotted a handwritten note, believed to be written by a child's parents, and it was seriously adorable.

‌



She said on Reddit: "Found in the ball pit at an indoor play place." In the image, it also showed the note which read: "Najiba. You are smart, kind and beautiful. I am so proud of you and you will have a great year! See you soon. Mom & dad."

‌



Sadly there wasn't much explanation as to who the people were in the note. But it's likely to have been written to a child who might have misplaced it in the soft play area.

Reddit users react to adorable message discovered in ball pit

In the comments section, other parents admired the cute gesture from the mum and dad to their child. One said: "I can't tell if I'm tearing up because of the sweet note or because that ball pit just gave me conjunctivitis."

‌



While another added: "That is lovely! I wish my parents had done things like this." To which the original poster replied: "Right! Gonna start leaving little notes like this for my kid once he can read. Maybe I'll just draw stuff he likes for now for him to find."

Looking for more stories?

Previously, a mum was left fuming when her neighbour stuck a rude note on her car with one detail which made her blood boil.

In a post on Instagram, Crystal Murphey, from the US, explained her son had driven his car to school and had secured permission from a resident near his school to park on the road outside her home.

Article continues below

But when he came back to his vehicle at the end of the day, he found a note stuck to the driver's side window, angrily telling him the area isn't an "overflow parking lot for high school students".

The neighbour hadn't just stuck the note down with tape - they'd actually superglued the letter to the window.

In the video, Crystal said: "I'm in shock. This is superglued on."

News.title: Gold coffin carried through streets as mourners gather for teen killed in M9 crash
News.content:
Gold coffin carried through streets as mourners gather for teen killed in M9 crash

Joe Carthy was one of five teenagers killed in the M9 collision which also left a child and three women seriously injured.

View 7 Images Joe Carthy was laid to rest in Athy, Co Kildare, on Friday (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire)

A gold coffin carrying one of five teenagers killed in a horror wrong-way motorway crash arrived by horse-drawn carriage as mourners gathered to say goodbye.

‌



Joe Carthy was laid to rest in Athy, Co Kildare, on Friday after he died alongside Jack Kennedy, Alex McCarthy, Jeremy O’Brien and Kamil Pustkowski in the M9 collision last weekend.

‌



Mourners wearing white T-shirts bearing an image of Joe followed his coffin into the church, while others carried framed photographs of the teenager.

‌



View 7 Images Joe Carthy was laid to rest in Athy, Co Kildare, on Friday (Image: Irish Mirror)

The five teenagers had been travelling in a BMW which was driven the wrong way down the motorway before colliding head-on with another car.

Ella Hendricken, Niamh Kinsella and Alma Kinsella, aged in their 20s and 30s, and a seven-year-old boy were travelling in the other vehicle on their way to Dublin Airport for a family wedding.

‌



Niamh and Alma Kinsella remain in a critical condition at Tallaght Hospital, while Ms Hendricken is being treated for serious injuries at St Vincent’s Hospital.

View 7 Images L-R : Ella Hendricken, Niamh Kinsella and Alma Kinsella were seriously injured in the M9 crash.

Gardaí maintained a visible presence in Athy during Joe’s funeral, with checkpoints on roads into the town and officers stationed around the church amid concerns over possible disorder.

‌



The priest extended “sincere sympathy to Joe’s family”, adding: “We gather with sorrow in our hearts.”

Outside the service, pictures and videos were displayed on a screen as music played. A blue carpet led to the church steps, with white flowers placed around the entrance.

A funeral mass for Alex McCarthy was due to take place at Holy Family Church in Askea, Carlow, on Friday afternoon.

‌



View 7 Images Joe Carthy was laid to rest in Athy, Co Kildare, on Friday (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire)

A vigil is also due to be held in Carlow on Friday evening in support of Ella, Niamh, Alma and the boy injured in the crash. A fundraiser for the family had raised more than €640,000 by Friday morning.

The crash has prompted renewed debate in Ireland over dangerous driving, social media content and the provision of State care for children.

‌



Earlier this week, Ireland’s child and family agency Tusla confirmed one of the teenagers who died had been in its care, while two others were known to the agency.

View 7 Images Joe Carthy was laid to rest in Athy, Co Kildare, on Friday (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire)

Tusla has committed to sharing information with the independent National Review Panel, which examines deaths and serious incidents involving children who were in State care or known to the agency.

‌



Government and opposition politicians have also criticised social media companies over content depicting dangerous driving and called for harmful material to be removed more quickly.

TikTok declined an invitation to publicly appear before the Oireachtas Media Committee on September 23 to discuss how it deals with content that “glorifies illegal activity”, instead offering lawmakers a private briefing.

The company said it would not be “possible” to appear while investigations by Gardaí and media regulator Coimisiún na Meán were ongoing.

‌



View 7 Images Joe Carthy was laid to rest in Athy, Co Kildare, on Friday (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire)

TikTok also said it would not be “appropriate” for it to be the only video-sharing platform called before the committee when similar content appears elsewhere on social media.

The company said it had removed all content flagged to it and banned accounts which breached its policies against criminal behaviour.

‌



It also said it removes content that glorifies violence or promotes crime that could harm others, while limiting the spread of material encouraging unsafe behaviour including dangerous driving.

Coimisiún na Meán has sought a “full account” of how TikTok is dealing with reports of illegal or harmful content and said it remains in “close contact” with An Garda Síochána.

View 7 Images The scene of the fatal M9 crash (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

‌



Meta, which owns Facebook and Instagram, has policies restricting users under 18 from seeing imagery depicting real-life dangerous driving likely to cause injury. It also bans content promoting criminal or harmful activities.

Snapchat said it had removed content relating to the crash for breaching its policies and would continue taking action against material depicting dangerous or illegal behaviour.

Irish Justice Minister Jim O’Callaghan has pledged to provide An Garda Síochána with “whatever resources they require” to tackle dangerous driving, including introducing pursuit-specific training for the first time.

‌



He said Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly will begin implementing the training this year.

Local Gardaí had earlier attempted to stop the BMW, but it failed to stop. A decision was later taken not to pursue the vehicle as it travelled the wrong way down the motorway.

Mr O’Callaghan is also exploring the introduction of a specific offence for deliberately driving against the flow of traffic on a motorway.

Article continues below

Opposition politicians have argued that problems policing dangerous driving stem partly from recruitment and retention issues.

Sinn Féin justice spokesman Matt Carthy said a “failure to address” Garda numbers is “fuelling a community safety crisis” across the State.

He added: “There is a clear shortage of community gardaí and interventions needed to prevent crime before it occurs.”

News.title: Prince Harry and six others face privacy case legal bill of up to £34.5m
News.content:
Prince Harry and six other public figures face paying up to Â£34.5m to the publisher of the Daily Mail after a High Court judge imposed an exceptional order for legal costs over their failed privacy case.

The seven claimants, also including Sir Elton John and Liz Hurley, must pay an initial Â£9.54m by Friday of next week to Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL).

The judge ruled that the case was a rare one in which the claimants should have to pay far in excess of the costs that had been agreed before trial, criticising how they presented their claims as "unreasonable to a high degree".

On 7 July, Judge Mr Justice Nicklin dismissed the claims of unlawful information-gathering, which ANL denied.

The Duke of Sussex and the other six claimants have until 2 October to attempt to launch an appeal.

Those other claimants are Sir Elton John and his husband David Furnish, former Liberal Democrat deputy leader Sir Simon Hughes, racial justice campaigner Baroness Lawrence, and actresses Sadie Frost and Liz Hurley,

They had insurance to cover up to Â£16.2m of Association Newspapers' costs in the event of losing the case - but Friday's ruling means the newspaper group could now try to recover up to the Â£34.5m that it said it had to spend to defend itself. This means the duke and others could face a bill of some Â£18m.

Justice Nicklin said: "I regard a claim for costs in excess of Â£34 million as, on its face, excessive and as giving rise to real concerns as to whether all of the costs now claimed by Associated were reasonably incurred and are reasonable in amount."

But he added he had "decided not to impose a ceiling on Associated's recoverable costs", as it would "be too broad-brushed, would risk unfairness, and would be vulnerable to the charge that it was arbitrary".

The judge also ruled that ANL's costs should be determined on an indemnity basis, which is more favourable to the publisher in terms of the amount it can recover, aside from where orders had already been made.

He added it was "striking" that "not a single allegation of serious wrongdoing was voluntarily withdrawn" by the group of seven claimants.

He said: "That matters. Serious allegations of criminality or grave impropriety cannot properly be left hanging over individuals in that way.

"If a party no longer advances such an allegation, or no longer has a proper evidential basis for advancing it, the allegation should be withdrawn clearly and in terms.

News.title: Girl, 6, dies days after Shoreham sea tragedy killed three family members
News.content:
A six-year-old girl has died in hospital after getting into difficulty in the sea off Shoreham in West Sussex, in an incident which also killed her father, mother and sister.

Saja El-Khawas, a British Palestinian from London, was pulled from the sea by emergency crews on Tuesday.

Her father Hassan El Khawas, 55, mother Zeina Alayn, 37, and 14-year-old sister Sara, died despite the efforts of paramedics at the scene.

Emergency services were called to the sea off Shoreham Fort at about 14:40 BST on Tuesday to a report of four people in difficulty in the water.

In a statement, Sussex Police said the family had travelled down from their home in London to visit Shoreham that day.

The force said the family had entered the water from the beach at Shoreham Fort about 14:00 before getting into trouble.

News.title: Meghan in talks for role in Netflix series The Gentlemen, BBC understands
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex is in talks to return to acting with a role in Netflix series The Gentlemen, the BBC has learned.

Discussions are in their early stages but this would be Meghan's first significant acting role since her marriage to Prince Harry.

Much of the two previous series of The Gentlemen, which was created by Guy Ritchie, have been filmed in the Cotswolds - the area it is rumoured Harry and Meghan will set up home when they return to the UK later this month.

The Gentlemen, starring the actor Theo James, is a comedy series about a duke who becomes a drug baron.

The details of the discussions and any role Meghan might be offered have not yet been revealed.

Actors Hugh Bonneville and Vinnie Jones have appeared in previous series of the show.

Meghan was best known in acting for her part in the US legal drama, Suits, in which she played lawyer, Rachel Zane, for seven seasons. Her last episode aired in 2018.

News.title: Under-fives and pregnant women told to avoid runny eggs when eating out over salmonella risk
News.content:
Vulnerable people are being warned not to eat under-cooked or runny eggs when they are eating out because of the developing salmonella outbreak.

The Food Standards Agency (FSA) told the BBC the under fives, over 65s, women who are pregnant and those with health conditions should avoid them along with freshly-made products that might contain uncooked eggs, such as mayonnaise, souffle and hollandaise sauce.

But the FSA said well-cooked eggs in restaurants, cafes and from takeaways were fine to eat.

It comes after the UK Health Security Agency declared a national outbreak of salmonella food poisoning after one person died and hundreds more fell ill.

It is thought imported eggs or dishes containing them are behind the outbreak.

FSA chief scientific adviser Ian Young said: "If people are eating out or consuming eggs or egg-containing products from cafes and restaurants then for those people in particular who are young, elderly, pregnant or vulnerable, it's important to make sure that any eggs or egg products that you consume in those settings have been very well cooked."

He described the outbreak as "unusually large and rapidly increasing", and added that "people need to be careful".

But he reiterated the message that it was fine for people to buy British eggs from supermarkets as chickens bred here are vaccinated against common strains of salmonella.

"There is no link to those eggs to this current outbreak," he added.

Mark Williams, chief executive of the British Egg Industry Council, said eggs from Britain were safe to eat when runny, even for vulnerable people, and were widely available in restaurants and cafÃ©s.

"Customers who want to enjoy a runny egg should simply ask whether British Lion eggs are being used," he said.

News.title: Supreme Court temporarily unfreezes Trump ballroom construction
News.content:
The US Supreme Court has temporarily allowed construction of the White House ballroom to move forward.

The decision on Friday by Chief Justice John Roberts, issued as a stay, will allow US President Donald Trump's $400m (Â£297m) project to continue as the high court mulls over a case aiming to halt it entirely.

The stay will remain in place pending further action from the court.

The case, originally filed by a preservation group that argues the project would become irreversible unless stopped immediately, was appealed to the high court after a federal appeals court had ordered work to halt earlier this month.

The appeals court ruled that Trump was a "temporary tenant" of the White House and could not make the alterations without congressional approval. It gave the administration two weeks to appeal the decision.

The National Trust for Historic Preservation, a preservation group, has led the lawsuit against the ballroom, arguing it is causing irreversible damage to a historical landmark.

"We are aware of the administrative stay," the group told the BBC on Friday. "To be clear, this is not a final decision on the merits of the government's stay application, and we await further action."

Trump posted on social media that he is grateful for the Supreme Court's decision, saying the new complex is "vital for National Security".

"It is something that Presidents have wanted for 150 years, and that the Military has been seeking for the last 100 years. Their wish will soon be fulfilled!" he wrote of the new ballroom on Truth Social.

The court's decision represents a victory - albeit perhaps a temporary one - for Trump, who has long argued that the White House needs a larger events space, and more recently, that it was important for his security.

Had the Supreme Court not issued a stay, or chosen to rule against the Trump administration, the White House would have been legally obligated to halt construction on Friday.

The president has asserted that the new ballroom was needed to accommodate grand parties and state visits and would improve security.

Government lawyers have argued the additional security complex and features included in the ballroom project are needed to protect the White House complex from drones, ballistic missiles, biohazards and other threats - changes essential to protecting the president, his family, and staff.

While initially billed as a 650-person ballroom that would incorporate the existing building when it was announced in July 2025, revised plans later expanded it to have a capacity of 900, and then about 1,000, with the entire structure of the East Wing being demolished in the process.

News.title: Murder investigation after wildfire uncovers body in park
News.content:
A murder investigation is under way after human bones were uncovered at a west London park following a wildfire, the Metropolitan Police said.

Emergency services were called to Bedfont Lakes Country Park in Hounslow at about 18:35 BST on Wednesday, 12 August.

A police spokesperson said the remains were found by a member of the public after the wildfire affected an area of woodland known as The Pits.

Following a post-mortem examination, police said the bones belonged to a woman aged between 25 and 45. They said it was not clear how long the remains had been there and officers were still working to identify her.

News.title: Watch: UK marks first national day for victims and survivors of terrorism
News.content:
The UK's first annual national day for those impacted by terrorism was marked today in a ceremony that took place in London.

Survivors of various attacks spoke of how their lives changed forever, including Paul Price, a survivor of the Manchester Arena attack, that claimed the life of his wife Elaine.

The Prime Minister Andy Burnham also spoke at the ceremony, he told survivors he had a 'deep admiration' for them.

The room also observed a two-minute silence and there were multiple musical interludes.

News.title: Arran ferry evacuated over 'bomb threat' by passenger rescued from sea
News.content:
A 23-year-old man has been arrested after a ferry service on Scotland's west coast was evacuated over a bomb threat.

Operator CalMac said a passenger was reported overboard on the MV Caledonian Isles 16:40 service, carrying 329 people from Brodick on the Isle of Arran.

The BBC understands that after being pulled from the sea by the ferry's rescue boat, the man then told crew that there was a bomb on board.

All passengers were removed on foot at Ardrossan so the vessel could be searched. Police Scotland said it was established that the threats "were not credible".

The passengers and others waiting at the port were taken to a nearby supermarket car park by police while the search was carried out.

After this was complete, officers allowed people back on board to collect their vehicles.

News.title: Ofcom investigating Sky News over Farage harassment claims
News.content:
Ofcom would not comment on any investigation but said it treated complaints in strict confidence and would not "publicly confirm the identities of individuals concerned".

Farage claims reporters from Sky News approached his daughter's home while he was out of the country.

Sky News says it did not interact with his daughter, and was trying to ask Farage about a Â£5m gift he received from cryptocurrency investor Christopher Harborne before he entered Parliament in July 2024.

A parliamentary standards investigation into whether the gift broke any rules resumed earlier this month after Farage was re-elected as MP for Clacton following a by-election he triggered that was boycotted by the other major parties.

Upon returning to the country, Farage was questioned by Sky News over the undeclared gift, to which he responded: "You tell your bosses, you harass my family any more, there will be serious consequences, that's what your organisation has done this morning, now go away."

When pressed on the donation again, he said: "Did you not hear me? You have broken all the rules, Leveson and everything else, cut."

At the time, Sky News said in a post on X: "Sky News was not at the property at 7.41am. As has already been acknowledged, and as shown in the footage from 10.19am, Sky News was outside a property where Mr Farage was registered to vote at the last election.

"Sky News did not interact with Mr Farage's daughter.

"On a single occasion, we approached the property without a camera operator, identified ourselves as Sky News and the adult occupant chose not to engage. We were seeking to contact Mr Farage to ask questions about the gift he accepted from Mr Cottrell.

"This is a well-established and routine journalistic practice when reporting on matters of legitimate public interest.

"The footage clearly demonstrates that Sky News did not 'hound' or pursue Mr Farage's daughter.

"At no stage did we seek to speak to anyone other than Mr Farage in connection with this story."

The BBC has contacted Sky News for comment.

Ofcom says it aims to conclude fairness and privacy complaints within 90 working days.

News.title: Men admit trying to tunnel into jewellery shop
News.content:
Three men who were caught trying to tunnel into a jewellery shop from a neighbouring massage parlour have admitted conspiracy to commit burglary.

Ioan Asafeti, 39, Laurentiu-Daniel Nitisoara, 38, both of no fixed address, and Sergiu Plastin, 42, of Portadown, County Armagh, were behind the attempted raid on Mitcham Road in Tooting, south London, in the early hours of 17 July.

Kingston Crown Court heard how body-worn camera footage captured Nitisoara being arrested in a nearby alleyway, while Asafeti was found hiding on a rooftop.

Plastin was tracked down using mobile phone data and arrested later that day at Stansted Airport as he tried to board a flight to Ireland.

News.title: Man denies charge over Manchester synagogue attack
News.content:
A man has denied failing to disclose information in relation to the Manchester synagogue attack.

Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim appeared before Westminster Magistrates' Court and pleaded not guilty to failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity.

The 49-year-old, of St James Road in Higher Broughton, Salford, spoke only to confirm his name and indicate his plea. He was remanded into custody to appear at at the Old Bailey on 25 September.

Worshippers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, a Syrian-born British citizen, drove into the gates of the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue on 2 October.

He then began attacking with a knife, while wearing a fake suicide belt, before being shot dead by police outside the synagogue.

News.title: Body recovered in search for man fallen overboard on cruise ship
News.content:
A body has been recovered in the search for a man fallen overboard from a cruise ship in the North Sea off the east coast of Scotland.

The man was reported missing at 08:35 on Ambassador Cruise Lines vessel MS Ambition, about 36 nautical miles from Arbroath.

Lifeboats, coastguard crews and aerial support were launched as part of a search operation before the ship docked in Dundee.

Police Scotland said formal identification was still to take place, but the missing man's family had been informed.

The ship was on its return journey to Dundee from a solar eclipse cruise, with stops in Iceland and the Faroe Islands.

It docked in Lerwick before returning to the city on Friday.

BBC Scotland News understands that the passenger's luggage was still onboard and his bed had not been slept in.

News.title: French becoming more effective in stopping small boat crossings, UK says
News.content:
French police tactics are becoming more effective in stopping small boats in the English Channel from reaching Britain, the Home Office has said.

It credits French authorities with intercepting 185 potential crossings involving 4,300 migrants this summer over four separate weeks, as well as stopping 12 boats at sea using new techniques.

Footage released by French police shows officers racing across a beach in jeeps to intercept a launch. Once the boat is abandoned, an officer slashes it lengthways with a knife.

The Conservatives described the announcement as a "joke" and said Channel crossing preventions were "down by half over the past year".

Migrants can be seen throwing objects at the officers, one of whom appears to respond with pepper spray.

While Channel crossings are down about 40% compared to last year, thousands of illegal migrants are getting through with 250 arriving on Monday.

In late July a record 165 migrants reached the UK in a single boat with Border Security Command pictured towing a mega dinghy - estimated to be the same size as a standard bus at 13m (42ft) long - when it arrived in Dover on 23 July.

The Home Office, citing French police figures, said that since it struck a deal with France three months ago which included additional funding for authorities, 61% of small boats have been intercepted - a five per cent increase compared to last year.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the "UK-France deal is already having a real impact".

The UK-France Border Security deal agreed in April under the Starmer government, includes Â£501m over three years to strengthen operations in northern France and Â£161m for new approaches.

Previously the French authorities allowed most dinghies to head towards the UK once they had launched, because of the risk of intercepting them in deep water, while loaded with people.

Of the 12 dinghies stopped so far at sea, three interceptions took place in the last two weeks.

The techniques being used have not been disclosed by the UK or France.

Charlie Eastaugh, director of maritime and small boats at the Border Security Command, told the BBC that "last Thursday alone, the French prevented all three of the boats that tried to cross".

Speaking to the BBC at the Western Jetfoil facility in Dover used to process migrants, he said: "Two of those they prevented at sea, and one they prevented on land."

News.title: Burnham to send high-performing civil servants to mayoral offices
News.content:
High-performing civil servants will be sent to work in mayoral offices in England, as part of the prime minister's efforts to transfer power from central government to local leaders.

The pilot scheme, due to start in the autumn, will see every mayoral authority get between five and 10 civil servants for a six to nine month period.

The 18 mayors will be able to request civil servants with the particular skills they need and Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the scheme would help communities "unleash and unlock their own potential".

The announcement followed a virtual meeting between local mayors and the prime minister, who was working from his new No 10 North office in Manchester.

A series of devolution deals over the past 10 years have seen mayoral authorities - made up of local councils and elected mayors - given power and funding over areas such as transport and housing.

Mayoral strategic authorities have been established in areas including Greater Manchester, the West Midlands and West Yorkshire but not in others, for example Surrey and Cornwall.

Further measures announced by the government include a new civil service fast stream pilot for local authority roles in Yorkshire and Humber.

The fast stream programme recruits between around 700 and 1,400 people each year, who are then placed across different government departments.

Applications for the new Yorkshire and Humber scheme will open in October with successful candidates starting in September 2027.

The Future Leaders Scheme - which provides training and support for senior civil servants - will be opened up to those working in mayoral and local authorities.

A digital devolution programme will create a data-sharing model between central government and mayoral authorities.

Burnham spent almost a decade as Greater Manchester Mayor and since becoming prime minister has repeatedly said he wants to devolve power away from central government.

During his leadership campaign, he announced he would set up a new Downing Street team based in Manchester, called "No 10 North".

The new unit, overseen by senior minister Louise Haigh, has been tasked with being the "dominant driver of the UK's economy".

Successive governments have said they want to move more civil servants out of London and last year ministers set a target to reduce the numbers of roles in the capital by 12,000.

According to the most recent figures, 19.6% of civil servants are based in London and the number has been gradually decreasing for the past four years.

Liberal Democrat local government spokesperson, ZÃ¶e Franklin MP, said: "Andy Burnham is again putting metro mayoral regions first with this staffing trial.

"Local authorities across the board should be given the same funding and staffing opportunities if he truly wants to grow every region in England."

News.title: Royal Mail misses delivery targets again but hails 'encouraging' signs
News.content:
Royal Mail has once again missed its delivery targets for first and second class post, but said it is making progress towards the goals as its turnaround plan continues.

The postal service delivered 85% of first class deliveries the next day between March and June, up from 76% in the same three months of 2025, but below regulator Ofcom's 90% target.

Second class mail was delivered within three days 91% of the time, another improvement from the previous year, but short of Ofcom's 95% target.

Royal Mail said the results are "encouraging and show that the work we are doing to improve the service is having an impact".

Royal Mail, which is owned by International Distribution Services (IDS), has struggled with rising competition in the delivery market, fewer people sending letters and fines from the regulator for missing targets in recent years.

But it said that, compared with the same period last year, the portion of first class mail delivered next-day had risen significantly while the amount of second class mail delivered within three days had improved slightly.

Chief operating officer Jamie Stephenson said: "These results are encouraging and show that the work we are doing to improve the service is having an impact.

"First Class performance is well ahead of where we expected to be at this stage of our Improvement Plan, while Second Class is tracking in line with the plan."

Stephenson added that there is "more to do", pointing to a Â£500m investment plan to improve the firm over the next five years. The plan includes a commitment to meet Ofcom's delivery targets by May 2027.

The postal service has faced years of criticism from politicians and the public over the slowness of its letter delivery.

It is currently under investigation by Ofcom for the second year running for failure to meet its delivery targets.

The regulator fined it a record Â£21m in October last year for missing targets in 2024-25.

In March, postal workers from across the UK told the BBC they were being asked to move or hide mail from senior bosses so it looks like delivery targets were being met.

The firm apologised to Gloucester residents where post was sometimes delayed for months, admitting its service there was "totally unacceptable".

Most recently, people in Worcestershire hit out over postal delays, complaining of weeks-long delays for important post to arrive, with some missing hospital appointments.

Royal Mail recently said it aims to meet regulator Ofcom's targets by May 2027 as part of a turnaround plan costing around Â£500m in the next five years.

"We know there is more to do," Stephenson wrote in a statement. "We are investing Â£500 million over five years and making significant changes across our network... None of this progress would be possible without the continued hard work of our frontline colleagues, including through the recent extreme heat."

IDS was bought in 2025 by Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky.

The residents of a Pasadena neighborhood are furious after a mail carrier allegedly beat a beloved local peacock with a rock after it followed him to his mail truck.

Gina Davis, a schoolteacher who lives in the neighborhood and has affection for the peacock, named Sugar, said she noticed the bird seemed disoriented and was refusing to eat or drink.

“Pretty much the entire neighborhood knows him, takes care of him,” she told the LA Times.

She told the paper she looked at her home security footage and discovered that a mail carrier had thrown a rock at the white-feathered bird and then struck the animal.

The video made its way around the neighborhood, shocking and infuriating the locals.

A peacock on a neighborhood street in California. A postal worker reportedly threw a rock at a peacock in Pasadena and then hit it with an object after it followed him back to his truck ( Getty )

Davis said after the mail carrier threw the rock at the bird it followed him back to his truck, at which point he hit it with a stick he had in his truck.

“The peacock was just standing in front of his truck,” Davis said. “He got out of his truck and had a club or stick or something and hit it.”

After discovering what happened, Davis' neighbor called Pasadena Humane and a veterinarian came to check on the bird. The peacock has since been taken to the group's Wildlife Center.

A spokesperson for the group told the LA Times that the bird was examined and beyond minor swelling where it was struck the animal does not appear to have suffered any broken bones.

Pasadena Humane said the peacock is expected to recover but will remain under observation for a few more days. The group is investigating the attack and is asking neighbors to provide any video footage they have of the incident.

Kristina Uppal, a U.S. Postal Service spokesperson, told the LA Times in a written statement that postal workers have had previous encounters with peacocks and that the organization is working with Pasadena Humane concerning the birds.

The statement also said that the USPS takes "allegations of inappropriate conduct seriously and will take appropriate action, as warranted, consistent with Postal Service policies."

The Independent has requested comment from the USPS.

Davis said she does not know if Sugar will be returned to their neighborhood, but told the paper she would be happy knowing the bird has a safe place to live.

Peacocks have become an increasingly common sight in cities and towns across California.

While the birds are beautiful, there have been numerous reports of neighborhoods struggling with their sometimes aggressive behavior. On top of large populations of the birds leaving waste in yards, public sidewalks, and city streets, they've also been known to scratch the paint on cars and damage homes.

Manchester United have made a £60m bid for Carlos Baleba as they look to make the Brighton player their third midfield signing of the summer.

They are yet to agree a deal, with Brighton thought to want a higher price for the Cameroon international, but talks are progressing.

United’s offer, which could rise by £5m, means they have resurrected their interest in Baleba, a player they first targeted last summer.

Brighton then valued the 22-year-old at over £100m, but were also reluctant to sell, but Baleba’s price has dropped after a difficult year.

United have turned back to him after missing out on two midfielders they liked, with Mateus Fernandes instead joining Tottenham from West Ham and Elliot Anderson moving to Manchester City from Nottingham Forest.

They had also agreed to sign Ederson from Atalanta before a medical revealed concerns and the deal for the Brazil international fell through.

While Baleba is currently out after an ankle problem, it is not thought to keep him out for long or to be enough of an issue to prevent a transfer from going through.

United have bought two midfielders in this transfer window, with Andrey Santos joining from Chelsea for £48m and Youri Tielemans arriving from Aston Villa for £35m.

But they have lost Casemiro while Manuel Ugarte is sidelined and Mason Mount has missed their last two-pre-season friendlies.

The past week, President Donald Trump has had to respond to and tamp down stories about Natalie Harp, his super-eager executive assistant who calls herself the “human printer.”

On Thursday evening, Trump biographer Michael Wolff released letters to The Daily Beast wherein Harp gushed to the president, “You are all that matters to me” and “no one knows or cares about me more.” The New York Times’ Maggie Haberman, perhaps the premier chronicler of Trump, has said Harp is “not beloved” by her colleagues in the White House.

Her estranged brother Preston burst out laughing on CNN the past week when he learned that his sister reportedly jumped into the trunk of a Trump motorcade SUV when there wasn’t room for her to sit during a trip to court in 2023. Then there was the story on MS NOW that Harp worked at the White House without a security clearance. On Thursday, First Lady Melania Trump made her first public appearance in a month amid reports she has refused to be anywhere Harp is, leading to her having a lower public profile of late.

“I heard you missed me,” she joked in her opening remark before adding, “Here I am.”

And all of this snowballed thanks to Sen. Jon Ossoff, the freshman Democrat from Georgia, who has become public enemy number one of the White House and plenty of other conservatives — merely for invoking Harp. And in doing so, he might have honed a skill Trump uses to maximum effect: occupying everyone’s attention and getting his opponents on the back foot.

open image in gallery Sen. Jon Ossoff caused a firestorm in Washington with his comments about White House executive assistant Natalie Harp. ( AFP/Getty )

Last week, Ossoff held a rally in Atlanta. These events have become something of an exhibition match for the 39-year-old senator who often clips videos from his re-election events that become catnip for liberals on social media.

The videos have generated talk not just about whether Ossoff will win by double digits this November, but whether he should seek the presidency in 2028.

This time, Ossoff rattled off an attack regarding the report that Trump left Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and the White House press pool on one plane as he faced a potentially deadly Iranian missile attack while he and Harp went on another plane.

“He golfs and trades stocks. See, he doesn’t want to do his job,” he said. “He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar.”

The line earned Ossoff applause in Georgia, but it earned him consternation from plenty of Republicans. Scott Jennings, the conservative CNN pundit who is reportedly lobbying to replace departing Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary, called Ossoff a “garbage human.”

And the response from the White House was even more vicious. White House Communications Director Steven Cheung called Ossoff “Jon J***off” and a “cuck,” and spokesman Davis Ingle called him “cringeworthy, feminine theatre kid cosplaying as Barack Obama.” Trump for his part calls Ossoff “Pee-Wee Herman.”

Even some Democrats, like former Obama adviser David Axelrod, chafed at the attack.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump’s administration has been on the defensive about his relationship with Natalie Harp ever since Ossoff’s attack. ( Getty )

But to borrow a phrase regularly used in the South, a hit dog will holler. Ossoff’s attacks would not have caused such a stir if he did not know it would make the White House lash out at him.

Unlike some other Democrats, Ossoff, who represents a state that voted for Trump twice, has made opposing the GOP standard bearer a cornerstone of his re-election campaign.

His record is not as liberal as his MS NOW-watching fans might want. He voted for the Laken Riley Act, which would allow for immigration authorities to detain non-citizens arrested for or chanrged with specific crimes. He also voted to confirm Marco Rubio to be secretary of State and for Trump’s crypto legislation.

Still, he has bet that Trump’s sinking approval rating due to the poor economy and the war in Iran will juice up turnout in the midterm election against his ultra-MAGA challenger Rep. Mike Collins. Even when Trump won Georgia, suburban voters in the Atlanta metropolitan area trended leftward.

He likely hopes to dominate his re-election campaign and shake off the image he has as an upstart amateur who narrowly lost a special election congressional race in 2017. And of course, as much as he says he is not thinking about the White House, he is a senator from a swing state. And South Carolina, home of Democrats’ first primary contest, is just a quick drive away.

Ossoff has lapped up the attention and expect him to post a massive fundraising number. Whether due to his age, the voters in his state or something else, he might be the only Democrat who has figured out how to turn Trump’s best weapon–media attention–against him.

News.title: Arsenal vs Coventry LIVE: Odegaard says Gunners ‘could have done better’ despite dominant win
News.content:
Can ANYBODY Stop Arsenal From Winning The Premier League Again

Arsenal got their Premier League title defence off to a dream start as they cruised past newly promoted Coventry City 3-0.

Kai Havertz opened the scoring against last year’s Championship winners, who are back in the top flight for the first time since the 2000/01 season, in the opening 15 minutes.

Bukayo Saka doubled the Gunners’ lead a few minutes later before Martin Odegaard finished off an emphatic job shortly after the restart, with Coventry keeper Carl Rushworth getting his fingertips to something of a miskick but unable to keep it off the line.

Mikel Arteta’s side were in cruise control throughout and put in another dominant showing after dismantling Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield last week, with World Cup winner Mikel Merino nearly adding a fourth in stoppage time.

But this was a dispiriting return to the Premier League for the Sky Blues, with Frank Lampard aiming to simply keep his team in the to flight this season.

Four wrap products have been withdrawn from shop shelves following concerns over bacterial contamination that could cause kidney failure and prove fatal.

Manufacturer Summit Foods is recalling the Snacksters Chicken Fajita Wrap, Snacksters Hoi Sin Wrap, East Street Deli Sweet Chilli Chicken Wrap and Target a Snack Chicken Fajita Wrap due to the potential presence of Shiga toxin-producing E.coli (STEC).

The action covers all items featuring use-by dates up to and including September 5 2026. The Snacksters Chicken Fajita Wrap was retailed at Iceland and Bestway Wholesale.

The Food Standards Agency (FSA) has urged customers who bought any of the wraps to discard them rather than eat them.

open image in gallery There are fears over E.coli contamination ( Getty Images/iStock )

The FSA noted that STEC can cause severe abdominal pain and diarrhoea. In certain instances, it may result in haemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), a condition capable of causing kidney failure and fatality.

Individuals experiencing symptoms are advised to stay away from nursery, school or work until at least 48 hours after they are symptom-free to reduce the risk of passing it to others. Informational notices will be displayed in stores and on websites selling the affected items.

Summit Foods said in a statement: "As part of our routine testing, we have identified a potential food safety issue affecting a small number of our wrap products.

"We are working closely with the authorities and our customers to recall the affected products.

"Consumer safety remains our highest priority. We are sorry for any concern or inconvenience this may cause."

It might be a recruitment drive with a difference for Michael Carrick. Perhaps Manchester United’s priority in the summer transfer market was to find the new Casemiro. In one respect, though, it was to get the next Michael Carrick. Twenty years after his arrival from Tottenham, the current manager may be the last central midfielder United have bought to prove a sustained success.

There are others who have prospered for a year or two – Casemiro, who had two fine seasons out of four at Old Trafford, is a case in point; Carrick’s teammates Anderson and Owen Hargreaves were, too, along with Paul Pogba, Ander Herrera, and maybe even Fred and Marouane Fellaini. There are others, like Manuel Ugarte, Morgan Schneiderlin, Bastian Schweinsteiger and Sofyan Amrabat, who were almost exclusively ineffectual.

In contrast, Carrick lasted a dozen years, played 464 games and was a linchpin for most of them. Perhaps, then, that first-hand knowledge of what it takes to operate at the heart of the United side made him the right man to identify a successor.

So far, two have arrived, Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa. United want a third addition, and have posted a £60m bid with Brighton for Carlos Baleba. Perhaps none is a direct replacement for Casemiro; but then, given the Brazilian’s idiosyncrasies, maybe no one could be.

Carrick is overseeing an overhaul. “I know we’ve got a good midfield,” he said. “We’ve brought in some really, really top players and really good characters, which is important. We’ve got to evolve and we’ve got to improve.”

He sounded satisfied, though some targets have proved elusive. A £35m move for Atalanta’s Ederson broke down when a medical revealed concerns about the Brazilian’s knee. United liked Aurelien Tchouameni, but he remains at Real Madrid. They wanted Mateus Fernandes, but Tottenham paid West Ham £85m for the Portuguese, and Elliot Anderson, but Manchester City splashed out £116m on the Nottingham Forest player. In each case, it was a bid that seemed to take United out of the reckoning.

open image in gallery Manchester United signed Youri Tielemans in a £35m deal from Aston Villa (Niall Carson/PA) ( PA Wire )

That may be a sign of how times have changed. Pogba cost a then-world record £89m; United may not be big spenders any more, may not be competing at the top end of the market. They got Santos for £48m, Tielemans for just £35m, due to a release clause. That felt like a bargain.

In the summer of the £100m midfielder – Sandro Tonali as well as Anderson, perhaps with more to follow – Carrick thinks United have found value for money.

“There’s certainly players that have been more expensive, I think that’s pretty obvious,” said Carrick. “We’re delighted with the two that we’ve brought in and for the money. But actually take that away, I’m delighted that we’ve got them. Two fantastic players give us really good balance, give us a lot within the team, offer us different things. So certainly for the value that we feel we’ve got, I think we’ve done very well with them two.”

open image in gallery None of United’s midfield acquisitions are direct replacements for Casemiro

Tielemans is an instructive case. He has joined at 29 and Carrick, 25 when he debuted, was no rookie when United signed him. The Belgian is a fine passer of the ball, just as his manager was. The sense, perhaps, is that Carrick’s vision of a midfield is more constructive than destructive; should it be Tielemans alongside Kobbie Mainoo, there is no real ball-winner. But the same may have been said when Carrick was paired with Paul Scholes. Carrick has also used Mason Mount in a deep midfield role in pre-season, though he is a fitness doubt now. Casemiro could be called a defensive midfielder; Mount rather less so.

Two decades ago, Carrick cost £16.8m, which struck some as excessive then, but proved money very well spent. Now the rather bigger price tags attached to other midfielders at least reflect a widespread recognition of the importance of the role. “The midfield connects the whole team together and has a big say on how the team performs with and without the ball, and the character and the personality of the team,” Carrick said.

Part of Carrick’s appeal on the pitch lay in his calmness and consistency. That, it seems, is what he wants in a midfield. “I think the foundation of the team is important to be consistent, to be consistent through one game from start to finish, to be consistent over a period of time,” he said. “You need a solid foundation through the middle of the team ... If you look at all the top teams over the years, all the great teams over the years, the spine of the team is really strong. So we’re conscious of that, and I think we’ve got a good spine of the team right now.”

They will need one. Perhaps the midfield reflects how and where United lost their way. Over 20 years, Arsenal and Chelsea, Liverpool and City had many a hugely successful signing in the centre of the park. United, given that Bruno Fernandes is more of a No 10, did not. In Tielemans, Santos and, maybe, Baleba, Carrick hopes he is changing that. And few are better qualified to judge a United midfielder than him.

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

There was another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimaraes, absent through injury, was certainly not needed here.

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.
