News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

Sports.title: Arsenal 3 Coventry 0: Champions fly out of the traps as Havertz, Saka and Odegaard inflict misery on Frank Lampard
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA claims Arsenal do not see themselves as defending the Premier League but are actually “attacking” another title.

Although this was the latest example of Arteta-speak, it does sort of make sense.



The Spaniard looks a different person now the weight has been lifted off his shoulders after guiding Arsenal to their first title in 22 years and his team look even hungrier to keep hold of the trophy.

After Arsenal wiped out Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield five days earlier, they enjoyed an effortless opening-day win over last season’s Championship winners.



Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard scored in a victory that was not hugely surprising, as Frank Lampard’s team were always likely to suffer a rough night.

The result gives us absolutely no idea how Coventry – back in the top-flight after 25 years – will get on this season and none of their fans should be worried about this in the slightest.

Equally, here this was an instant, brutal lesson in what happens when you lose the ball cheaply in defence or your goalkeeper makes an error, like Carl Rushworth did on a couple of occasions.

It is obviously early days. But if the first two games are anything to go by, which includes the trip to Cardiff, the handbrake is definitely off an Arsenal team who are playing with both freedom and real menace.

It looks as though Arteta is even letting the players enjoy themselves, which was not always the case.

It also helps they have recruited well so the Gunners look even stronger.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

New arrival Ezri Konsa, a terrific signing, was unveiled before the game while there was also a huge cheer for £34million winger Christos Tzolis who responded by having a hand in the opening two goals.

Bruno Guimaraes is the showpiece signing but a groin injury means he must wait before appearing in the Premier League for Arteta.

While many Arsenal fans are still dreaming of another big arrival in attack, they should not get too excited.

It seems that Julian Alvarez is unlikely to happen, certainly at this stage, and a few players could be leaving north London.



So even if they do not sign anyone else, Arsenal fans should not be greedy and instead, be happy with what they have got.

As for Coventry, we should salute their remarkable rise.

On the corresponding weekend nine years ago, they lost 1-0 at home to Newport in League Two.

Lampard has spent about £130m on nine players but only four of them started and keeper Rushworth and Frank Onyeka were on loan from last season.

Former Frankfurt defender Aurele Amenda featured at centre-back while ex-Burnley winger Loum Tchaouna was out wide on the right and the team will have been glad to get off the pitch without a humiliation.



It did not help their cause that Arsenal started with a real swagger.

It is interesting that Havertz once again started ahead of Viktor Gyokeres.

The German did not have a great season as he was injured for half of last term and then spent a lot of time on the bench making only seven League starts.

Havertz’s frustration in the dressing room at London Colney, watching Gyokeres start games, was noticeable.



But he started the Champions League final and has got this season off to a flyer, following up his goal against City with the first of the season in the 15th minute.

Tzolis, who had a goal-bound shot blocked by Bobby Thomas, lost the ball, won it back and poked it to Riccardo Calafiori.

He produced a bobbling pass to Havertz who, as a result, did not manage the cleanest of strikes but it was still enough.



Arsenal’s second was a gift by Rushworth who has just completed a £22.5m move from Brighton after spending last season on loan at Coventry.

Some in the goalkeeping community believe he could potentially become one of Thomas Tuchel’s top three keepers in the England squad but he will have to do better than this.

He pushed a deflected Tzolis cross into the path of Saka who had an easy chance although Declan Rice deserves all the credit for a surging run.

Rushworth will also be angry with himself for failing to keep out Odegaard’s goal four minutes into the second half but he was caught out by the fact the Arsenal skipper mishit his shot after a pass from Ben White.



The ball squirmed apologetically into the net but Odegaard did not care.

Hilariously, he has now equalled his entire Premier League tally from last season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And the way he is playing, he could also score quite a few more because he, too, looks a different player from the one who struggled with form and injury.

The season has continued where it left off for Arsenal, though, and the rest of the Premier League should be afraid. Very afraid.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Christos Tzolis leaves Emirates breathless with stunning Prem debut but Gabriel Magalhaes quiet
Sports.content:
ARSENAL started their title defence in style as they brushed newly promoted Coventry City aside with ease.

The Gunners cruised to a 3-0 victory over Frank Lampard‘s Sky Blues to start the new season exactly where they ended the last one – top of the league.



Kai Havertz opened the scoring with a sweeping finish into the bottom corner.

The German’s goal was followed by a tap-in from Bukayo Saka, who was started his first match since the World Cup.



And it was captain Martin Odegaard who put the cherry on top for Arsenal when he sliced home the third to cement all three points.

Here’s how SunSport Arsenal reporter Joshua Hall rated each individual performance…



DAVID RAYA – 6

Very little for the Spaniard to do given Coventry’s lack of threat, but comfortable whenever called upon.

BEN WHITE – 7

Took up some good spaces between Martin Odegaard and Bukayo Saka when Arsenal were attacking.

His overlapping run and dragged pass put the ball on a plate for Odegaard’s goal.

There’s no doubt that Jurrien Timber will be a miss for Arsenal in these opening few games, but White is more than capable of deputising for the Dutchman.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

CRISTHIAN MOSQUERA – 7

New signing Ezri Konsa was paraded on the pitch before kick-off and will probably be stepping straight in to take Mosquera’s place next week.

But Mosquera did nothing to warrant being dropped in this showing, keeping Coventry at bay with some assured defending.

GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 6

A quiet night for the Brazilian who had little to do at the back.

Unusually, he struggled in the air – losing every one of his four aerial duels.

RICCARDO CALAFIORI – 7

Going forward there are few better full-backs in Europe than Calafiori.



His sweeping cross to find Kai Havertz for the opener was an example of what he can offer Arsenal in the final third.

DECLAN RICE – 7

A first start since the World Cup for Rice after new signing Bruno Guimaraes was ruled out with a groin injury suffered during the Community Shield.

His galloping run through the midfield was the driving force behind Arsenal’s second goal and an reminder of how good a fit and rested Declan Rice can be.



MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 7

Mikel Arteta said Lewis-Skelly will “100 per cent” be staying at Arsenal this summer during his press conference on Thursday.

Another good performance from the Hale End graduate proved just why Arsenal would have been mad to sell him.

Assured, combative and confident.

MARTIN ODEGAARD – 8

Last season Odegaard was off the boil and battling injury for most of the campaign, this year he looks hungry.

The Arsenal captain was the metronome against Man City last week and this was another encouraging performance.



Smart slide passes and little flicks were accompanied by his first goal of the season – albeit from a mis-hit effort.

BUKAYO SAKA – 7

Was positioned perfectly to tap the second goal into an open net and double Arsenal’s lead.

If Saka can shake off his achilles problems this season then he will undoubtably be amongst the top contributors in the Premier League at the end of the campaign.



CHRISTOS TZOLIS – 8

What a home debut. At £34m, Tzolis looks like an absolute bargaim.

The Greek ace was ridiculously sharp on the ball and constantly trying to make things happen.

His dogged pressing won Arsenal the ball back for the opening goal and it was his cross that led to the second, too.

He looks like he will be an output machine.

KAI HAVERTZ – 7

A brilliantly taken first goal from Havertz, who guided Calafiori’s pass into the bottom corner with ease.



The German made it look simple, but it was a terrific finish to open his account for the season.

There was no chance for Viktor Gyokeres to come off the bench against his former team, with Havertz playing the full 90 minutes.

Perhaps a glimpse at the pecking order in N5 this season.

You have to wonder how many minutes Zubimendi will get this season given Lewis-Skelly’s form and the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino ‘plotted U15s World Cup hosted next to DISNEYLAND with 211 teams representing every Fifa nation’
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO reportedly tried to launch an Under-15s World Cup next to Disneyland featuring all 211 Fifa nations.

The under-fire Fifa chief is said to have plotted a youth “festival of football” inspired by Little League in baseball.



Infantino – who is already facing calls to resign after trying to sell off chunks of the World Cup – was hoping to commercialise the U15 tournament.

The event would have taken place at the ESPN Wide World Of Sports Complex close to Disneyworld in Orlando, Florida, according to the Athletic.



But the plans were scrapped just before the start of the senior World Cup this summer.

Proposals for the tournament were drawn up by businessmen such as ex-Mexico FA chief Juan Carlos Rodriguez, the report says.



Organisers spoke with broadcasters ESPN, who have aired the Little League World Series, to discuss hosting it at their Disney complex.

And proposals also included having the opening and closing ceremonies at the Disney theme park.

Infantino was also involved in the plans, the report goes on to say, and wanted the opening match to be between Israel and Palestine.

It comes after his failed attempts to get the two federations to shake hands at the Fifa Congress in April amid the nations’ ongoing conflict.

Infantino first discussed the idea for the new U15 event in December with shorter matches and smaller pitches, but never spoke about commercialising it.

The Swiss chief said at the time: “We have been very active in promoting youth competitions and development, and this is a natural next step, and a very joyous one.”

Infantino remains under immense pressure after his failed bid to create a subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would have overseen the World Cup and allowed investors to claim a stake in it.



He quickly lost support from a number of organisations and federations, including Uefa – who threatened a boycott of Fifa tournaments.

They were joined by Concacaf and the AFC, while the English FA and Welsh FA have revoked their support for Infantino.

Infantino has had support from some federations, including Mexico, Qatar and Argentina.

He is likely to face stiff opposition ahead of the Fifa presidential elections on March 18, 2027.

Uefa chief Alexander Ceferin is said to be a candidate, as well as PSG chief Nasser Al-Khelaifi, Arsene Wenger and Concacaf chief Victor Montagliani.



It comes as Fifa start the process of deciding the World Cup 2038 and 2042 hosts, with the UK set to bid to host one of them.

Sports.title: Wolves fans’ fury as woke club bosses ban iconic pre-match anthem played for DECADES over the F-word
Sports.content:
WOLVES fans hit out yesterday after club bosses banned their favourite ­pre-match anthem because it encourages swearing.

The Liquidator by Harry J Allstars had been played for decades at the Championship side’s Molineux Stadium.



But Wolves bosses, acting on police pleas, have axed the tune said to prompt chants of “F*** off West Brom” against their rivals.

Supporter John Millar, 69, said: “The fans are furious. They’re passionate and this obviously won’t stop swearing at games.



“It’s made worse by the fact West Brom still play The Liquidator and swear at us, and are now laughing at us for being so woke.

“The song hasn’t been played before games for a while but I’d support a campaign to bring it back. It has always been part of our tradition and fires us up.

Fellow Wolves fan Ryan Gill said: “It’s utter woke nonsense and we’ve missed an open goal.

“I’m not sure how telling another club to f*** off is discriminating but that’s today’s world we live in . . . soft as s**t.”

Ryan’s brother Joe said: “The one chance they get to bring the whole stadium together and fans back on side and they’ve fumbled it.”

Supporter Rob Morris added: “It makes the higher-ups at Molineux look weak and unwilling to listen to the fans, which is nothing new with this current ownership”.



Wolves executive chairman Nathan Shi, appointed by Chinese owners Fosun, said: “I respect what The Liquidator means to many Wolves supporters.

“But we also have a responsibility to make decisions based on where the club is today and the standards we expect around our matchday environment.”

The Liquidator will be played at West Brom’s Hawthorns when the sides clash in February.

Yesterday Twitter account The Albion Way mocked: “Fair play to Nathan for respecting our pre-game song. He knows there’s only one team worthy of using it round here.”

Chelsea are believed to be the first club to play The Liquidator, a catchy reggae instrumental, in 1969.

Sports.title: Premier League is not a charity – rest of football must put away its begging bowl if it wants to attack the golden goose
Sports.content:
EVERYONE seems to agree the Premier League has too much money, too much power and too much influence.

And, apparently, it is all getting terribly unfair. Funny that.





Because there is another way of looking at the Premier League’s wealth and power. It is the reason an awful lot of the rest of English football has any money at all.

I have spent more than 30 years in football, much of that time as a Premier League executive and shareholder sitting around the table when the arguments about money, governance, distribution and the future of the game were being had.

Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

So, I have seen the Premier League from the inside. It is not perfect but it’s close to it.

Yet I do find it rather strange that we spend so much time complaining about the Premier League’s success while simultaneously asking it to pay for everyone else.

You cannot have it both ways.

The Premier League committed £1.6billion to the wider game and communities from 2022 to 2025.

In 2024-25 alone, more than £550million went beyond the Premier League itself. More than half a billion pounds. In one season.

That money reaches all 92 Premier League and EFL clubs, all 72 National League clubs, women’s and girls’ football, grassroots football and communities.





SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Since 2000, more than 1,000 clubs have benefited from the Premier League Stadium Fund to the tune of more than £200m.

This isn’t a league sitting in a vault counting its money while the rest of football picks over the crumbs. It is the golden goose everyone appears determined to tell off for laying golden eggs.

There are real arguments about how the money should be distributed.

Should the EFL receive more? Almost certainly worth discussing.

Are parachute payments right? Debate away.

Is competitive balance perfect? Of course not.

Does the Premier League have too much influence? That’s a legitimate question.

But if we are going to have those arguments, let’s at least start with the inconvenient truth.

The Premier League’s success is funding a huge part of the game beneath it. And this is where the comparison with Fifa comes in.



I have heard the Premier League compared to Fifa — an organisation supposedly interested primarily in money, power and protecting its own interests. Really? Let’s look at what each actually does.

The Premier League has to run football every week. Not a five-week tournament every four years. EVERY WEEK.

Players such as Elliot Anderson need to be paid. Managers have to be paid. Coaches, doctors, analysts, academy staff, everyone else needed to put on the world’s most commercially successful domestic football competition need to be paid. And then there is the small matter of the players . . . they don’t play for free.

Premier League clubs scout them, sign them, develop them, train them and pay them. They carry the enormous cost of producing the football product that everybody else wants a piece of. Even Fifa.

When international football comes calling, clubs must release their players when the regulations require it.

There is no polite conversation along the lines of ‘would you mind letting us borrow your £100m player for a few weeks? The answer, effectively, is: hand him over.

The club keeps paying him. Fifa gets the player and Fifa compensates the club, but to what level? Let’s look at the numbers.

For the 2026 World Cup, Fifa’s Club Benefits Programme has a headline value of $355million — that is about £260m.



Sounds enormous… until you put it beside the cost of actually running a Premier League club.

Of that Fifa figure, $100million is allocated to clubs releasing players for World Cup qualifying matches while $250 million relates to clubs whose players participate in the finals.

The remaining $5m is reserved for programme administration and ‘other purposes’ — which is wonderfully vague. What purposes? Your guess is probably as good as mine.

That entire Fifa pot is distributed around the world’s clubs.

Manchester City’s 2024-25 accounts showed that £355.4m was spent on wages and salaries alone.

So Fifa’s $100m qualifying pot is less than a third of Manchester City’s annual wages.

One club. One year. That puts the financial burden of producing football into perspective.

Fifa does not pay the club wages of the players it uses for international football. The clubs do. And that is why the comparison is worth making.

Not because Fifa and the Premier League are the same — they plainly aren’t. But because it exposes how simplistic the accusation against the Premier League can be.



Premier League money doesn’t just disappear into Premier League pockets. It pays for the product.

And then a huge amount of it goes back into football. That is why I find the constant outrage about Premier League power slightly curious.

If you want less Premier League money, fine. But understand what that means.

Less money for the EFL and National League. Less money for grassroots facilities, for women’s football and the communities that benefit from Premier League funding.

The Premier League is not a charity. It is a highly successful business. But its commercial success is the engine that allows it to make such a substantial contribution to the rest of the game.

You cannot keep attacking the golden goose and then complain when the eggs get smaller.

And you certainly cannot accuse it of being interested only in money while simultaneously putting out your begging bowl.

Of course, the Premier League is interested in money. It would be spectacularly badly run if it wasn’t. The difference is what it does with that money.

After more than three decades in football, including many years sitting around the Premier League table as a shareholder, I have seen clubs fight fiercely for their own interests. Of course they do. Football is a business.



But I have also watched the Premier League become the most successful football competition in the world.

And its success created a financial engine that reaches far beyond the 20 clubs actually playing in it.

So, by all means challenge the Premier League. But let’s stop pretending its success is somehow the problem. For a huge part of English football, it is the solution.

And if you want to compare it with Fifa, do so. But just remember one thing.

The Premier League doesn’t get its money from nowhere. It earns it.

It pays the players. It carries the risk. It puts on the show. And then it gives away an extraordinary amount of its success.

So perhaps the question shouldn’t be: Why is the Premier League so powerful? Perhaps it should be: What would English football look like without its money?

I suspect a lot of the people complaining about the Premier League’s power would rather not find out.

Sports.title: ‘He’s a future England manager’ – Jamie Carragher heaps praise on Premier League boss on first day of new season
Sports.content:
JAMIE CARRAGHER has insisted Frank Lampard will be a future manager of England.

Speaking ahead of the Premier League curtain-raiser between Arsenal and Lampard‘s Coventry, Carragher gushed with praise for his former England team-mate.



Lampard’s last visit to the Emirates as boss came during his second spell as Chelsea manager, which ended in a 3-1 loss for Lampard’s Blues.

That stint had followed a poor one at Everton which left the Toffees in relegation danger by the time he was sacked.



But since then the 48-year-old has turned a corner in his managerial career after successfully guiding Coventry to Premier League promotion.

Carragher told Sky Sports: “It’s a rollercoaster – being a player or manager. Unless you are the absolute elite and you seem to win every week or do really well.



“For me what Frank Lampard has done is come back from a couple of knocks and shown he’s a really good manager.

“But I think he’s a future England manager, I really do.

“I think the England manager should be English, that’s why I’m saying that as well.

“But when you think of where he’s managed; he’s been in the Championship, he kept Everton up, very close to bringing Derby up, even at Chelsea he did brilliantly in his first season then came back and I was commentating on that game and it was hard to watch.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“But all those experiences that he’s had are what make him the manager he is now.”

Lampard has urged his Coventry stars to play without fear this season as they play their first Premier League campaign for 25 years after celebrating the Championship title.

He said before facing the English champions: “The last thing I would like to have after a game against Arsenal – or any team like this – is a regret of our approach and that we didn’t give it everything.

“If we can do that as a team, then we will compete in this league and show teams what we are.

“If we don’t, we’ll be disappointed. I’ll remind the players of that [before the game].



“I want to show in our performance and in how we approach the game that we haven’t come into it with any kind of fear.

“We respect Arsenal greatly, but it doesn’t mean you play with too much respect and you’re passive.

“I want us to go there with the right mentality and approach the game in the right way.”

However, Lampard’s team had to endure an early baptism of fire at the Emirates after going 2-0 down inside 25 minutes.

Sports.title: Olympics legend Usain Bolt joins unique SUNDAY LEAGUE team as he follows in footsteps of multiple Prem icons
Sports.content:
USAIN BOLT has followed the lead of a number of Premier League icons by joining Sunday league side Wythenshawe Vets.

The former world’s fastest man, 40, is a footy fanatic who even had a stint with a professional club in Australia‘s top tier, scoring for the Central Coast Mariners in a friendly.



He has also trained with Borussia Dortmund and Norwegian side Stromsgodset in his hunt to spark a career in the sport in the late 2010s.

But now he has found a new footballing home as he registered to play with the Manchester-based club, which competes in the Cheshire Veterans football league.



But Wythenshawe Vets are far from your average Sunday league side, boasting the talents of a number of top retired footballers over the years, thanks to the recruitment efforts of ex-Manchester City man Stephen Ireland.

The likes of Marc Albrighton, Papiss Cisse and Danny Drinkwater are among the stars to have turned out for the side.

Also registered to the club are Antonio Valencia, Joleon Lescott, Maynor Figueroa and Emile Heskey, among other top-flight stars.

Bolt toyed with the idea of getting involved in the unique weekend project earlier this year.

When asked on talkSPORT about the prospect of joining the side, he said: “Listen, I’m ready. I’m ready. If I get into some shape, I’m ready to go.”

The Jamaican sprinter is an eight-time Olympic gold medalist, and holds the current world records in both the 100m and 200m events.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

And its fair to say that the defenders of the over-35 Cheshire vets league might still struggle to keep pace with the forward today.

Bolt has kept himself in top shape since his retirement, and is a regular fixture for World XI at charity football event Soccer Aid, whom he has both captained and, most recently, managed.

If there was ever an environment where the pressure off, this could be it for the star.

Wythenshawe vets have produced some memorable light-hearted moments, such as Cisse’s 30-second nightmare in which he saw a penalty saved and sent the subsequent corner straight out of play before it had even reached the penalty box.



Manchester United fan Bolt will just be sad that Wayne Rooney never responded to his invite to play with the side.

Bolt once harboured aspirations of featuring for the Red Devils himself, but came close when he captained World XI at Old Trafford during Soccer Aid 2023.

Sports.title: Man Utd AGREE £70m Carlos Baleba transfer just hours before first game of season as they finally land Brighton star
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have agreed a £70m deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

The midfielder, 22, has long been linked with Old Trafford and the Red Devils have finally got their man.



United’s second bid of £65 plus £5m in add-ons has been accepted by the Amex and the player travelled to Manchester on Friday night for a medical.

Baleba is expected to sign a five-year deal with an option of an additional year and the Seagulls have inserted a sell-on clause.



However, he is currently sidelined with an ankle injury sustained in Brighton’s pre-season friendly against Strasbourg.

Talks reopened after tests confirmed that the injury Baleba suffered in early August was less severe than first feared, with an expected return date in late September.



It ends a long-running transfer saga after United’s failure to sign the player last summer, when Brighton were said to be quoting an eye-watering £120m.

The discounted deal means United have managed to save themselves £50m on Brighton’s initial price.

Baleba has been eager to join United since the Red Devils first showed interest last summer.

He went on to suffer an indifferent for the Seagulls after his failed move.

Sports.title: Arsenal deliver on Mikel Arteta's promise as defending champions flatten Coventry
Sports.content:
Arsenal deliver on Mikel Arteta's promise as defending champions flatten Coventry

ARSENAL 3-0 COVENTRY: Gunners get their Premier League title defence off to a roaring start, with Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard all on the score sheet

View 3 Images Kai Havertz got Arsenal under way early on (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

This was a statement victory to leave the rest of the Premier League in no doubt.

‌



Arsenal already look like the team to beat as the reigning champions made it a miserable night for Frank Lampard’s Coventry in their first game back in the top flight for 25 years.

‌



The Gunners were rampant as they overran Coventry while utilising the full depth of their impressive squad as Kai Havertz, Bukaya Saka and Martin Odegaard were all on target in what became a precession at the Emirates.

‌



Arsenal will undoubtedly face more difficult tests in the weeks and months ahead, but the message was loud and clear: they are ready to defend their title.

The Emirates lapped it up as suddenly last season’s nerves have been replaced by an overwhelming sense of confidence that they have the best team in the top flight.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Mikel Arteta has spent the past few weeks talking about how his reigning champions are hungry for more success. And this felt like a performance to underline Arsenal’s ambition and determination for the campaign ahead. They were strong, focused and dangerous as they gave newly-promoted Coventry a nasty welcome back to the top flight.

Arsenal looked in the mood from the start and already looked stronger than last season. New £51million defender Ezri Konsa was paraded before kick-off while £75m midfielder Bruno Guimarães was missing because of a minor thigh issue.

But, again, much of the performance and damage was done by another new boy, £34m winger Christos Tzolis, who carried on from where he left off with his two assists and man-of-the-match award in the Community Shield.

‌



These days £34m is seen as underwhelming with fans clamouring for bigger names and yet Arsenal may just have unearthed a gem in Tzolis. He looks strong, physical and inventive.

View 3 Images Martin Odegaard pulled the strings for Arsenal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

It was Tzolis who closed down Coventry right back Milan van Ewijk, Riccardo Calafiori put over a low cross and there was Havertz to sweep home in the 15th minute. That was a dream start for Arsenal and a nightmare for newly-promoted Coventry. Lampard’s best laid plans to keep things tight were in tatters.

‌



It got even worse seven minutes later. Declan Rice powered forward from midfield, the ball was spread wide to Tzolis and the Greece winger sent over a low cross which Coventry’s £22m keeper Carl Rushworth could only parry. There was Saka in position to fire home from close range to give Arsenal a two-goal lead.

It is incredible that Rice and Saka finished World Cup duty with England just 34 days ago - and yet they were straight back into Arsenal’s starting XI after what must have felt like a mini-break.

And the assist was courtesy of Tzolis. Incredibly, the Greece international has now either scored or provided an assist in 21 of his last 22 games.

‌



The only exception was Arsenal’s friendly with Como when he scored the winning penalty in the shoot-out. Incredibly, that was Tzolis’ sixth assist in an Arsenal shirt, including pre-season friendlies.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis has started brightly in an Arsenal shirt (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Rice curled a shot just wide before half time and the gulf in class between the champions of the Premier League and last season’s Championship could not have been more stark.

Article continues below

It got even worse for Coventry and Rushworth after the break. Saka and Odegaard combined nicely, Ben White cut the ball back from the by-line for Odegaard.

The Arsenal captain mis-hit his shot, it deceived Rushworth and crept into the net. It was a horrible moment for the Coventry keeper. Odegaard’s goal also levelled his return from the whole of last season.

Sports.title: Arsenal hammer Coventry to send ominous message to Premier League rivals - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Arsenal hammer Coventry to send ominous message to Premier League rivals - 5 talking points

ARSENAL 3-0 COVENTRY CITY: The champions sent out an ominous message to their Premier League rivals as the likes of Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka scored in a rampant win

View 4 Images Arsenal made light work of Coventry to begin their season with three points

Arsenal made light work of newly promoted Coventry as the champions began the defence of their title with minimal fuss to go top of the table.

‌



The Gunners were handed the chance to kick off the season and needed only a quarter of an hour to score the first Premier League goal of 2026/27 as Kai Havertz got the ball rolling at the Emirates.

‌



The German, who only started seven league games last term as injuries plagued him, was able to sweep home first time after being found by Riccardo Calafiori, who seized on a Coventry error.

‌



Arsenal's second came just seven minutes later as Bukayo Saka was able to tap into an empty net from seven yards. Coventry were outclassed throughout and it would take them 85 minutes before they registered an effort on target.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The hosts only needed three minutes of the second-half to score their third as Saka and Ben White teamed up down the right to eventually find Martin Odegaard, whose scuffed shot was still enough to beat Carl Rushworth, who should've done better.

‌



Coventry were able to prevent the floodgates opening as they kept Arsenal scoreless for the final 40 minutes in the capital, even if they offered nothing in attack. Easier assignments await, starting next week against Hull, whilst the Gunners know tougher tests are to come.

Here's five talking points from the Emirates.

Arsenal irresistible

It is easy to say they were playing a newly promoted team, but Arsenal wore their champion tag with a real swagger. It is the first time since 2004 that the Gunners began the year as the Premier League's premier club - on that occasion they hammered Everton 4-1.

‌



View 4 Images Bukayo Saka doubled Arsenal's lead in the first-half

22 years on and they looked equally as impressive, taking control from minute one and sending an ominous message to the rest of the league. Tougher tests are of course to come, but Arsenal could not have hoped for better on opening night.

Coventry's tough first day

They say every day is a school day, and the Premier League new boys were dealt a tough lesson. They claimed the Championship title last term but after only 22 minutes in north London were two goals down and, effectively, having to look to next week for their first hope of points.

‌



A clearance that was blocked ultimately led to Arsenal's opener, no doubt Milan van Ewijk will wonder why he didn't just boot the ball into Row Z. Most promoted teams often have to be on the receiving end of a one-sided encounter in the opening weeks to truly understand what they're up against - Coventry had theirs on day one.

View 4 Images Frank Lampard's Coventry were dominated from minute one in north London

Havertz takes the initiative

The German endured an injury-hit campaign last year but was straight back into the team once fit, scoring in the Champions League final. On Friday Havertz got the nod over Viktor Gyokeres, who was sat watching from the bench when he saw his team-mate sweep home the Arsenal opener on 15 minutes.

‌



A lot of the Arsenal questions have been answered, but the champions are seemingly still undecided over whether Havertz, a false 9, is the man who can take them to the next level ahead of a natural striker in Gyokeres. Goals will ultimately prove the biggest decider and Havertz has the starting berth, which he looks set to keep.

Odegaard's classy reminder

Once upon a time Odegaard was Arsenal's undisputed No 10, everything good about their attack ran through him. Then he sustained the odd injury and Arteta continued to invest in players who were capable of filling his playmaking role, and all of a sudden there's been questions over the Norwegian's future.

View 4 Images Martin Odegaard was central to Arsenal's attacking quality

‌



It almost felt as though the ex-Real Madrid star knew that people had raised the debate over whether he should command the start he did several years ago, but based on this performance few, if any, can argue that Odegaard remains one of the classiest operators in England, let alone Arsenal. Ironically his strike which saw him get on the scoresheet was perhaps his worst touch of the night, still, they all count.

MLS looks a stayer

Ever since the news broke that Myles Lewis-Skelly had been offered to Manchester United and Chelsea the versatile midfielder has been an ever present. Arteta insists he wants to keep the academy star and, despite the reports linking him with an exit, Lewis-Skelly looks every bit part of the fabric.

He played in the latter weeks of pre-season, started in the Community Shield win and played from the beginning against Coventry. Seeing him leave would no come as a massively surprise. The same though can't be said for Ethan Nwaneri.

The latest transfer news and rumours from the Premier League and around the world as deadline day edges closer

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba to Man Utd transfer details as medical set after breakthrough in Brighton talks
Sports.content:
Carlos Baleba to Man Utd transfer details as medical set after breakthrough in Brighton talks

Manchester United have a full agreement with Brighton over the signing of midfielder Carlos Baleba, who will travel this weekend to undergo a medical

View 2 Images Carlos Baleba is heading to Manchester United (Image: Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Manchester United are poised to sign Carlos Baleba after Brighton agreed a fee and gave him the green light to travel for a medical on Saturday.

‌



United have been interested in Baleba for over a year and now have a deal in place for the 22-year-old midfielder. After seeing an initial offer of £60million plus £5m in add-ons rejected, the two clubs have shaken hands on £65m plus £5m in add-ons, reports the Manchester Evening News, with a sell-on clause also included in the deal.

‌



Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos have already joined United this summer for a combined total of £85m, but manager Michael Carrick has always wanted a third player. United first enquired about Baleba last summer, only to be put off by Brighton's £100m asking price for the Cameroon international.

‌



A much lower-key 2025/26 campaign has seen his value decrease and United have moved to secure his services, having already agreed personal terms. He will travel up to Manchester this weekend and become their fourth major signing this summer, after Tielemans, Santos and Karl Darlow.

Baleba will have to wait for his United debut, however, after picking up an ankle ligament injury during Brighton's 0-0 draw against Tromso in their Conference League qualifier on Thursday.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler was asked about Baleba during his pre-match press conference on Friday. "He's a Brighton player. Like I said, I'll never comment on any rumours that are currently in the media, it's also something I definitely can't control," the German said.

"A lot of things are written, I know about situations but again, in two days I have a very important game together with my team and with my staff. We want to have a good start in the Premier League season, that's the only focus we have at the moment."

‌



View 2 Images Manchester United are long-term admirers of Carlos Baleba (Image: Getty Images)

Carrick has been vocal about the need for new arrivals in midfield this summer following the departure of Casemiro and the long-term injury suffered by Manuel Ugarte.

"I just think we're looking to strengthen the squad," he said when asked about Baleba ahead of their Premier League opener against Hull this weekend. "We're certainly working towards that, making the most of the situation that we have and trying to improve things and trying to move forward.

"You know, I said the same thing to you last time. So yeah, certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it. And I think we're in a good way to doing that so far."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta explains Bruno Guimaraes' injury problem as he misses Arsenal vs Coventry
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta explains Bruno Guimaraes' injury problem as he misses Arsenal vs Coventry

Bruno Guimaraes joined Arsenal in a £75million transfer from Newcastle this summer but is absent from the matchday squad for their opening Premier League match against Coventry

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes arrived at Arsenal for £75m but is unavailable (Image: Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes is missing from Arsenal's squad to face Coventry after picking up a groin injury on his debut for the club.

‌



Arsenal's new £75million signing made his debut for the club when he started their 3-0 win against Manchester City in the Community Shield last Sunday. But he suffered a knock and was replaced by Declan Rice at half-time.

‌



He was not in the squad named by Arteta for Friday's Premier League opener against Coventry, with Myles Lewis-Skelly starting in midfield alongside Rice. Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi are both on the substitutes' bench.

‌



"He had a slight tension in his groin," Arteta told Sky Sports. "He hasn't done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that game and we had to take him out. It's a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit."

In his pre-match press conference on Thursday, Arteta was asked about Guimaraes and replied: "Let's see how he is. He's evolving really well, but let's see for tomorrow."

The Gunners have signed Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for £51million to provide cover for Saliba. The 28-year-old England international's arrival was announced on Friday. He has signed a four-year contract and could make his debut against his former club.

Sports.title: Man United set for transfer windfall thanks to sell-on clause as player in 'advanced talks'
Sports.content:
Man United set for transfer windfall thanks to sell-on clause as player in 'advanced talks'

Manchester United's transfer funds could receive a boost before the end of the summer window as they benefit from a deal agreed in 2024

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's Man United transfer kitty could receive a boost (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Manchester United are set to see their transfer funds boosted when Willy Kambwala finalises his departure from Villarreal. Kambwala, 21, is on course to join Italian side Como and United will cash in thanks to having the foresight to include a sell-on clause.

‌



Como are looking likely to pip Spanish club Osasuna to his signing and the Red Devils will pocket. United sources described the sell-on clause for Kambwala as "sizeable" when he departed the club two years ago after making his debut aged 19.

‌



However, Villarreal are only expected to take in a modest fee, limiting the amount that United will receive. Kambwala departed Old Trafford in 2024 when the Yellow Submarine came in for the player.

‌



Villarreal tabled an offer of €5.5million (£4.7m) plus €6m (£5.14m) in add-ons to acquire Kambwala from United. The agreement incorporated a buy-back option and matching rights for three years, alongside the sizeable sell-on clause.

United occasionally included clauses in player sales prior to Sir Jim Ratcliffe's investment in the club, but it has since become standard practice following Ineos taking charge of football operations It is now a crucial part of negotiations when players head out of the club.

United included a "high percentage" sell-on clause and buyback option in the sale of Tyler Fredricson to Lausanne-Sport, with comparable clauses also written into the sale of Radek Vitek to Middlesbrough.

‌



United inserted a buy-back clause into the deal with Boro, along with matching rights and a sell-on clause of up to 35 per cent to profit from any potential future sale. Ethan Williams was transferred to Peterborough last week, with United inserting a 50 per cent sell-on clause into the agreement, alongside a buyback option and matching rights clauses.

Ethan Ennis completed a permanent switch to Stockport County earlier this week. United included a 50 per cent sell-on clause in that deal, as well as buyback and matching rights clauses.

View 2 Images Willy Kambwala left Manchester United in 2024 (Image: Getty)

‌

"I just think we're looking to strengthen the squad," he said. "We're certainly working towards that, making the most of the situation that we have and trying to improve things and trying to move forward.

Sports.title: Arsenal transfer 'proof' revealed live on Sky Sports in Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr claim
Sports.content:
Arsenal transfer 'proof' revealed live on Sky Sports in Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr claim

Arsenal's transfer for Vinicius Junior ended in disappointment for Gunners fans, but there has been an interesting revelation during a broadcast live on Sky Sports

View 3 Images Ian Wright said he has 'proof' Vinicius Jr was signing for Arsenal

Sky Sports pundit Ian Wright has claimed he has "proof" Vinicius Junior was set to move to Arsenal this summer. The Gunners were engaged in a high profile transfer pursuit of the Brazilian, which ended with the forward signing a new contract at Real Madrid.

‌



It was a fascinating saga for football fans which saw plenty of toing-and-froing during the negotiations. With Vinicius' move now not happening, Arsenal are now pursuing Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez.

‌



However, as Wright briefly started speaking about the Argentinian, he insisted Vinicius was, at one stage, on his way to Arsenal, despite both Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher appearing unconvinced.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Neville asked a leading question about Vinicius to Wright at the start of Sky Sports pre-match coverage of their Premier League opener against Coventry City. After Neville said: "Who are they bringing in?" Wright replied: "This is what I am saying.

"They were talking about...I don't know if Alvarez is coming. Obviously, then went for Vini, I know that was happening, people laughed at me. You two laughed."

‌



After Carragher snapped back: "That was never happening" Wright then replied: "At some stage, Ill show you, I'll show you the proof."

View 3 Images Vini Jr remained at Real Madrid amid interest from Arsenal (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Wright did not divulge what exactly his proof was in regards to Vinicius, at one stage of the saga, heading to Arsenal this summer. He signed a new six-year deal to remain at the Bernabeu instead of moving to north London.

‌



Vinicius Jr was the second big name attacker to snub Arsenal, after Morgan Rogers opted to move to Chelsea for £117m. The Gunners have now switched their focus to Alvarez, which is proving to be another drawn out transfer saga.

Atletico did not include him in their La Liga opener against Malaga, after Diego Simeone stated the World Cup winner was not in the right frame of mind to compete.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal pursued a move for Vinicius Jr (Image: 2026 The Arsenal Football Club Plc)

‌



After Wright told Carragher and Neville about his transfer "proof" he then added: "That's where we're going. I don't think we need to change the way we are playing, I just think we need to bring in that calibre of player to force it home."

One new signing who is already exciting Arsenal fans is Greek winger Christos Tzolis. His arrival from Club Brugge took place somewhat under the radar, as Arsenal were in the middle of the Vinicius and Rogers transfer sagas.

Sports.title: Arsenal kick off title defence with thumping win over Coventry
Sports.content:
Arsenal made a flying start to their Premier League title defence with a 3-0 thumping of newly-promoted Coventry City in the season opener at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners showed their readiness to go again with an impressive demolition of Man City in the Community Shield last weekend and they sent another statement to their rivals for the crown with this demonstration of dominance.

Coventry's unwanted stat Coventry became the first team to have no touches in the opposition box or make a tackle in the first half of a Premier League game, since Opta started collecting that data in 2007.

Once again new signing Christos Tzolis shone. The Greece international notched two assists at the Principality Stadium and was involved in Arsenal's first two goals on his Premier League debut, first winning the ball back for Riccardo Calafiori to tee up Kai Havertz and then sending in the cross Coventry 'keeper Carl Rushworth diverted into Bukayo Saka's path. "What a left-winger Arsenal have got," purred Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher on co-commentary.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kai Havertz fires Arsenal in front against Coventry as the Gunners begin their title defence

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bukayo Saka doubles Arsenal lead

This was a reality check for Coventry on their return to the top flight after 25 years away. They failed to make a tackle in the first half - they could not get near Mikel Arteta's men. It did not get much better for them after the interval, with Martin Odegaard's miscued finish adding a third for Arsenal just four minutes into the second period.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Odegaard nets the third for Arsenal

With Ben White, Saka and Odegaard combining brilliantly through the right channel, Tzolis electric on the left, and Havertz looking sharp ahead of some slick midfield play from Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly, Arsenal already look up to speed and formidable.

Where was Guimaraes? New Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes was missing with a thigh injury he picked up in the Community Shield win over Man City.

Their defence was barely tested but Ezri Konsa's pre-match welcome, following his £55m move from Aston Villa, was a reminder they have brought even greater strength and depth to that department, too. Tougher tests are to come, but they are going to take some stopping.

Coventry, meanwhile, will be relieved they do not have to face Arsenal again until April. They host Hull City next weekend in a fixture which will carry far more significance for their season.

The key moments from the Emirates

5: SHOT! Tzolis shoots over after cutting inside from the left flank.

7: OVER! Saka's shot is deflected over after Tzolis pops up on the right.

8: CLOSE! Tzolis is involved in everything Arsenal do in attack but sends his second shot of the game over after a well-worked short corner.

9: OVER! Declan Rice shoots over from 25 yards as Arsenal make a fast start.

15: GOAL! Tzolis wins the ball off Milan van Ewijk deep in Coventry territory, Calafiori crosses low for Havertz and the striker sweeps in a fine finish to give the Gunners the lead.

23: GOAL! Rice and Odegaard combine in midfield and Saka is perfectly placed to tuck in when Tzolis' cross is diverted into his path by Coventry 'keeper Rushworth.

Image: Havertz celebrates scoring the opening goal with Saka

34: CHANCE! Arsenal work the ball into the Coventry box and White is onto it but sees his shot blocked away. Coventry scrambling.

43: SHOT! Loum Tchaouna's overhead kick from the edge of the box loops onto the roof of the Arsenal net.

45+1: CLOSE! Rice whips a shot beyond the far post after another short corner.

49: GOAL! Odegaard, Saka and White combine through the right channel before the captain's miscued shot deceives Rushworth and adds Arsenal's third.

Image: Odegaard celebrates his goal

53: SAVE! Rushworth tips a curling effort from Lewis-Skelly over the bar for a corner as Arsenal keep their pedal to the metal.

66: SHOT! Tzolis stings Rushworth's palms with a drive from the edge of the box from an Arsenal corner.

90: SAVE! Rushworth is at full stretch to prevent Havertz arrowing in a fourth after some neat footwork from the Arsenal striker.

Sports.title: McIlroy heads back to range after slipping off BMW Championship pace
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy was heading straight to the driving range after slipping off the pace during round two of the BMW Championship in St Louis.

The Masters champion began with a fine six-under-par opening round for a share of the lead, but could only improve his total by one shot on Friday with a 69.

"I feel like conditions were pretty similar to yesterday," McIlroy told the Golf Channel.

"The wind was coming out of a different direction, but still very scorable. The greens are soft, maybe the ball's got a little bit more run out on the fairways, but you'll still see guys shooting pretty good scores today.

"I didn't quite hit it as good as I did yesterday, so probably an afternoon on the range for me.

"I'm proud of how I just hung in there. A lot of good par putts on the back nine, especially. The only bogey I had was with a mistake on the par-five eighth hole, but I made some really good par saves coming in and that sort of kept me in it."

Speaking about the fans at Bellerive, six-time major champion McIlroy added: "They're amazing, that's one of the biggest things I remember from being here in 2018 for the PGA was just how many people showed up and what a great atmosphere it was to play in.

"Yesterday was amazing for a Thursday. Today, teeing off at 9:45 on a Friday morning and the people out there were incredible. Looking forward to more of the same over the weekend."

Image: JJ Spaun looks set to run away with the second round

American JJ Spaun looked set to run away with the second round after he moved to 11 under at the turn.

Three bogeys on the back nine checked his progress but two birdies, including one at the last, left him as clubhouse leader of the early starters on 10 under.

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler, who was two over after a first-round 72, bogeyed the first hole but recovered well after the turn with five birdies leaving him still in contention at three under.

Sports.title: Man Utd agree £70m deal for Baleba
Sports.content:
Manchester United have agreed a £70m deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

The deal is worth £65m guaranteed, plus £5m in add-ons, and Brighton have also inserted a sell-on clause.

Baleba is expected to sign a five-year-contract with Manchester United and will undergo his medical in the next 24 hours.

Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they had enquired about signing him during the January transfer window.

He remained one of United's top targets this summer and will become their third addition in midfield after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

One source has told Sky Sports News when United looked to pursue Baleba last summer - they were quoted an initial price higher than the fee Moises Caicedo cost when he joined Chelsea in 2023, which was £100m, plus £15m in performance-related add-ons.

Despite Baleba's undoubted dip in form for Brighton last season, officials at United are understood to be happy with the deal 12 months on as they have had a long-standing interest in the player.

When will Baleba make United debut?

Baleba is recovering from an ankle ligament injury he picked up during pre-season and Sky Sports News understands he is due to be fit around the middle of September.

Manchester United face Manchester City on September 13 and Fulham on September 20, followed by the three-week international break which will allow Baleba ample time to acclimatise to life at Old Trafford.

Is Baleba a major gamble or a game-changer for Man Utd?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' William Bitibiri explains exactly what Baleba might bring to Manchester United's midfield

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

A year ago, Baleba appeared to have the world at his feet.

A breakout season at Brighton had established the then-21-year-old as one of the Premier League's most coveted young midfielders, with a move to one of Europe's elite clubs seemingly inevitable. Manchester United were among those interested, having identified Baleba as a potential transformative presence in midfield.

But Brighton's reported £100m-plus valuation proved a stumbling block. The move never materialised and Baleba stayed at the Amex.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Baleba's Premier League best bits

His form subsequently dipped dramatically. His numbers fell and, at times, he looked a shadow of the midfielder who had generated so much excitement the previous season.

That makes this a gamble for United. But, stylistically, there are few midfielders better suited to what they need.

Image: Baleba was among the league's leading defensive midfielders during the 2024/25 season - can he revive that form?

United require greater authority in the middle of the pitch and, crucially, someone capable of winning the ball back in deeper areas. Baleba brings exactly that. His athleticism, aggression and ability to carry the ball through midfield would add a level of dynamism and steel that is currently missing.

Santos and Tielemans have been astute additions, but Baleba offers something different: specialist defensive power coupled with the athleticism to drive United up the pitch.

His age is another major factor. Baleba is still only 22 and, despite his inconsistent season, there remains a belief around him that he can develop into one of the world's best midfielders.

That ambition is reflected in his influences. Baleba has spoken of his admiration for Paul Pogba, Yaya Toure and Andres Iniesta, while Neymar and Ronaldinho were among his favourite players to watch. There is a desire for self-expression in his game that goes beyond the physical qualities that made so highly rated.

There is risk attached to signing him. United would be betting on the player Baleba can become rather than simply the one he has been over the past 12 months.

But if United want to find a midfielder capable of growing into one of the best in his position, this is exactly the sort of gamble they should be willing to take.

Sports.title: Stokes makes impact with bat and ball for Durham
Sports.content:
Ben Stokes hit a half-century and took two wickets for Durham against Derbyshire on day two in the Rothesay County Championship.

The former England captain scored 53 from 61 balls, hitting 11 fours, before he was caught and bowled by Anuj Dal.

After helping Durham post 283 in the Division Two fixture, Stokes struck with his very first ball to remove Harry Came, who edged to Alex Lees at third slip.

Then a yorker accounted for Caleb Jewell as Derbyshire closed on 127-6, trailing by 156.

Olly Stone took 6-44 as Division One leaders Nottinghamshire ousted Surrey for 162.

Joe Clarke (37 not out) and Jack Haynes (34 not out) then put on 70 as Notts closed on 147-3 to lead by 169.

Second-placed Somerset enjoyed a fine day, posting 469 all out thanks to James Rew's unbeaten 74 and 48 from last man Migael Pretorius in a stand of 72.

Jack Leach then took 4-37 as Essex were skittled for 158, and although they were 59-0 after following on, with Dean Elgar unbeaten on 30 and Paul Walter 29 not out, the deficit was 252.

Image: Chris Woakes was in impressive form with the ball for Warwickshire

Chris Woakes took 4-36 as Warwickshire, in third, dismissed Sussex for 156.

But the hosts also struggled with the bat, scoring just 161 before an unbeaten 32 from Tom Haines left Sussex 84-3 second time around.

Yorkshire lost Adam Lyth for 51 and then nightwatchers Ben Cliff and Jafer Chohan as they closed on 131-5 in their second innings for a lead of 111 against Hampshire.

Glamorgan's Mason Crane top-scored with 44 as 15 wickets fell at Grace Road, Leicestershire finishing with a lead of 78 with eight second-innings wickets in hand.

Back in Division Two, Zak Crawley followed up his season's-best 81 on day one with a second-ball duck on day two but Kent closed on 38-2 and lead Middlesex by 139 runs.

George Bartlett scored 92 batting with the tail to take Northamptonshire from 134-6 to 284, before Lancashire closed on 68-2.

Rehaan Edavalath hit 63 and Brett D'Oliveira was unbeaten on 49 as Worcestershire, having dismissed Gloucestershire for 150, reached 205-7.

Sports.title: Root: England's bowlers don't know how good they can be
Sports.content:
Joe Root was thrilled by the performances of his bowlers as England's pace attack dismissed Pakistan for 135 before tea, to seal a statement three-day victory in the first Test at Headingley.

Pakistan were bowled out for 171 in 48.1 overs on day one, with England responding with an insuperable 409, as they romped their way to victory by an innings and 103 runs, in what was a dream start for Root in his second spell as captain.

On day three, Ollie Robinson (3-29), Jofra Archer (3-50) and Josh Tongue (3-43) seized full advantage of a worn Headingley pitch as they took three wickets apiece, while Gus Atkinson (1-11) followed up with a wicket of his own.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England head to Lord's 1-0 up in the series after beating Pakistan in the first Test by an innings and 103 runs

Root hailed his bowlers after the victory, claiming they "don't know just how good they can be".

"I don't think our bowlers understand well that they complement each other in these conditions, and what they're capable of doing," the Yorkshireman said.

"It's really nice for them to see that and to start the series like that."

Archer, who went wicketless in Pakistan's first innings, got England off to a flying start, dismissing both Pakistan openers, Azan Awais and Imam-ul-Haq inside four overs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer got England off to a flying start on day three, dismissing both Pakistan opening batters Azan Awais and Imam-ul-Haq

Tongue and Robinson were prolific throughout the match, with both completing eight-wicket hauls.

Robinson, the pick of the bowlers, has now won man-of-the-match awards in the two Tests he has played this summer, and Root hailed the 32-year-old for his ability to keep threatening Pakistan's batters late into the match.

"I thought Robinson was brilliant," Root said.

"The fact that he's still as effective in the second innings, having bowled 18 overs, and his understanding of what his requirements are in different phases of the game is important.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The England captain hailed man-of-the-match Ollie Robinson for his exceptional performance

"For him to be effective as the pitch changed throughout and to consistently keep asking difficult questions is a really good sign for us."

'It's always important to win a Test match'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After a four-year hiatus, Root enjoyed a dream return as England captain, but said things were different

After a chaotic few months, following the departures of former captain Ben Stokes and head coach Brendon McCullum, Root, who was trapped lbw for 66 on day two, stressed the importance of the victory.

But he added England were eager to "not get too carried away".

"It's always important to win a Test match," Root said.

"You're playing for England, right? It's what you set out to do every time you walk out on to that field.

"It's more the fact that we delivered on everything we spoke about, that's the most pleasing thing and the most enjoyable thing about all of it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root was dismissed for 66 runs off 112 deliveries on day two

"There's also an understanding that this is one game; there's going to be other challenges and different things to manage. That's the exciting part, and it's taking the confidence from this and being skilful to deal with that next thing, which will be Lord's."

After returning to captain England following a four-year hiatus, Root said things were different this time around.

"It was quite easy on occasion to leave Jimmy Anderson and Stuart Broad to it," Root said, reflecting on his previous spell as captain. "Very experienced, they knew how they were going to operate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue also impressed with the ball taking eight wickets during the match

"There's a lot of different things this time round.

"I'm very different as well. With everything going on around the Test match it was important to give as much clarity and simplicity to what we were trying to achieve and we delivered on that brilliantly."

Root in contact with Fleming every day

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stephen Fleming is set to take charge of England after the Pakistan series

Root also revealed incumbent England head coach Stephen Fleming has been in contact with him "every day".

Fleming will not take up the new role until after England's three-match series against Pakistan.

"He's kept tabs on things," Root said.

"It's just been great to have him on the end of the phone and I can speak to him as much or as little as I like.

"It's great that he's very invested already in what we're trying to achieve and there's been constant communication with Marcus Trescothick and me."

Sports.title: Brighton reject £60m Liverpool bid for Minteh
Sports.content:
Brighton have rejected a £60m bid from Liverpool for winger Yankuba Minteh.

Sky Sports News understands the proposal did not meet Brighton's valuation after the Reds previously failed with a £50m bid for the 22-year-old.

Minteh is currently unavailable due to an injury, which is likely to keep him out until October. Brighton are also without Kaoru Mitoma, who has been sidelined since May with a hamstring injury.

Brighton are also in talks with Manchester United over the sale of Carlos Baleba, with an agreement understood to be close over a deal worth in excess of £60m.

Liverpool prioritising reinforcements out wide

Reinforcing in wide-forward areas has been Liverpool's priority throughout this window after already signing Victor Munoz from Osasuna earlier in the window.

As part of Liverpool's process to add in wide areas, they are looking at a number of possibilities, one of those being Minteh.

Liverpool have been pursuing Bradley Barcola at Paris Saint-Germain and remain in contact with the European champions over a deal.

However, PSG's £145m valuation is a complicating factor as Liverpool do not currently want to reach that figure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Transfer Talk podcast panel discuss Bradley Barcola's potential move to Liverpool and whether or not the French forward would live up to the big money expectations.

Hurzeler: It's normal to have players linked with moves

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler says it is normal for players to be linked away with moves given the success of the Seagulls across recent season.

Minteh and Baleba are the latest Brighton players to attract transfer interest, after already losing Jan Paul van Hecke to Tottenham and Danny Welbeck to Chelsea earlier in the window.

Speaking ahead of their season opener against Aston Villa on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, Hurzeler said: "We know in general, all the players who there are rumours about are important players, they've been part of the journey over the last two years.

Sports.title: Kevin Blake's York tips: Ebor Festival day four picks
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing's Kevin Blake reveals a trio of picks as York's Ebor Festival concludes with yet another wildly-competitive card on day four on Saturday.

York have been unlucky with the weather this week, and the softening ground has created some extra challenges, but all being well we can hopefully finish the week on a high.

The Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (1:50) is the first race of interest, and one that looks overpriced is the Hamad Al Jehani-trained Archivist. Long-term readers may recall that I put him up as my selection in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot and while it didn't work out for him on the day, he gained compensation on his very next start when overcoming what was considered a near impossible draw of 20 in the Golden Mile at Glorious Goodwood.

Not only did he overcome his draw, he did it with a bit to spare and that performance signalled his readiness to be competitive at stakes level. This course and distance should suit him well and any ease in the ground shouldn't be overly inconvenient for him. He is drawn a little wider than ideal, but that is bearable given his price is so big. A big run from him wouldn't at all surprise.

The Sky Bet Constantine Handicap (4:10) is another extremely tough sprint handicap, but I'm game to have a swing at the Andrew Balding-trained Dance In The Storm. The manner in which the betting markets have been so positive about her in her four starts this season has strongly suggested that she is considered better than a handicapper.

While she has won two of her four starts over seven furlongs this season, she has very much been shaping as though she is worth a try at this shorter trip. She has a career-high mark to overcome, but this different distance could well unlock notable further improvement. She is a really interesting contender and warrants support.

The final selection of the week comes in the concluding Sky Bet Dav Reid Finale Handicap (5:20), and it is the Ger Lyons-trained Diego El Queso. The four-year-old has a progressive profile, winning a handicap at Leopardstown in good style back in April prior to having an absence of 12 weeks that suggests he may have had a hold up.

He returned to action with a tremendous run to finish second to Thread Of Gold in a valuable handicap back at Leopardstown and that form has been well advertised by the winner since then. He was well fancied for a similar race to this at Glorious Goodwood, but the race went wrong for him, yet he still managed to catch the eye in finishing sixth.

He is capable of better than he was able to show there and with both this course and distance and the ease in the ground all promising to suit him, he can be expected to make a bold bid for compensation.
